commands.name: agents
commands.summary: Create agents and change what they answer with, from their draft to the version people talk to
commands.description:
An agent answers people's questions from the knowledge bases it is given. Each agent has a draft, which is what
you change, named versions saved from it, and live, the version people talk to. Change the draft
(agents draft), save it as a version and compare it with live (agents versions), then publish it; publishing an
earlier version again rolls back, and agents history records every change to live.

To keep agents as files in a repository, use export, diff and apply instead: they read and write the same
drafts.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

examples.line: caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@v13 --expected-live v12

Each says which version it is with. Only the caller's own conversations, and those shared with it, are listed.

commands.name: agents draft
commands.summary: An agent's draft: the version you edit
commands.description:
The draft is the agent's working copy: every change goes here first, and nobody talking to the agent sees it
until it is published. Read it, change members with update, replace it whole, or edit it in your editor; send
the ETag you read with --if-match so you never overwrite someone else's change. When it's ready, save it as a
named version (save) or publish it straight away (publish). reset throws the draft's changes away.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

examples.line: caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --set guidance.instructions="Quote the clause you relied on."
caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name november-candidate

commands.name: agents draft compare
commands.description:
Compares two versions of an agent, member by member.

Returns one change per member that differs, from `version` to `with`, each with its value before and after; `before` is absent for a member `with` added, and `after` for one it removed. Lists are compared by their items' keys, so a path reads `workflow.phases[intake].transitions`. Both versions need the same access as reading them.

commands.name: agents draft diff
commands.summary: Compare a draft file with the agent's current draft
commands.description:
For one agent, without a folder: compare a draft file you're editing (from agents draft get -o yaml) with the
agent's draft before you replace it. For a folder of agents, use caitlyn diff.

Compares a file (as agents draft get -o yaml writes it) with the agent's current draft, member by member: lists
are compared item by item. Nothing is changed. --fail-on changes exits 3 when they differ, for a CI check.

To compare two stored versions, use the server's own comparison: caitlyn agents versions compare AGENT@v11 --with v12.

commands.name: agents draft edit
commands.summary: Edit an agent's draft in your editor, and save it when you close the editor
commands.description:
Opens the agent's draft in your editor ($VISUAL, $EDITOR, or `editor` in configuration) as YAML. When you save
and close it, the CLI shows what changed and replaces the draft, sending the ETag it read, so a draft someone
changed meanwhile is refused (exit 7) rather than overwritten. Nothing is published: save or publish the draft
when it's ready. For changing one member from a script, use agents draft update --set instead.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

commands.name: agents draft get
commands.summary: Read an agent's draft, with its full configuration and its ETag
commands.description:
Reads the draft, the version you change, with its full configuration and the ETag to send with --if-match when
you change it, so someone else's change in between is refused rather than overwritten. The draft is readable
only by the people and groups on the agent's version access grant; anyone else gets 404. To read what people
talk to, use agents live get; a saved version, agents versions get AGENT@name.

Acts on the version draft.

Needs:
  agents.aliases.read (scope agents:read).
  Returns 404 when it isn't shared with you. People and API clients.

Impact: Reads only.

When it fails:
  404 NOT_FOUND                A version name that does not exist, or that the caller may not see.  Exit code 6.

Available from Caitlyn 5.149.0.

commands.name: agents draft publish
commands.description:
Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it, so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is `rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

commands.name: agents draft replace
commands.description:
Replaces the draft with a whole configuration; `If-Match` is optional.

The draft becomes exactly the configuration sent, with defaults for every absent member: this is how configuration kept as code is applied. Every reference is checked as UpdateDraftVersion checks it, and a configuration over 256 KiB is refused with 400 `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE`. Returns the draft and its new ETag.

The draft's configuration becomes the configuration of `from`, which is a version name or `live`. Nothing else changes: `from` is kept as it is, and live is untouched. Returns the draft and its new ETag.

commands.name: agents draft update
commands.description:
Edits the draft with a partial update of its configuration.

Members that are absent stay unchanged, nested objects are merged and lists are replaced whole, each item taken as sent with defaults for its absent members. To return a member to its default, name it in `clear`; naming a member that is not clearable, or one the same request also sets, is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. A draft whose configuration would pass 256 KiB is refused with 400 `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE`. Returns the whole draft and its new ETag.

The live history records each publish and rollback: which version went live, which it replaced, who did it and
their note. Read it to see what people were talking to at a given time, or before rolling back.

commands.name: agents history get
commands.description:
Gets one live history entry, with the configuration live had after the change.

The configuration is that of the entry's `version`, which never changes. Reading the entry (who changed live, when, and to which version) needs agent read; its `configuration` needs what reading that version needs, so a caller without the permission to read versions, or without the agent's version access grant, gets the entry without it. It is also absent when that version was deleted through an older API that does not protect versions named in live history.

commands.description:
Versions are named, unchangeable snapshots of an agent's draft. Compare two before publishing, publish one to
make it live, or publish an earlier one again to roll back. --expected-live names the version you expect to
replace, so two people publishing at once can't silently overwrite each other.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

Compares two versions of an agent, member by member.

Returns one change per member that differs, from `version` to `with`, each with its value before and after; `before` is absent for a member `with` added, and `after` for one it removed. Lists are compared by their items' keys, so a path reads `workflow.phases[intake].transitions`. Both versions need the same access as reading them.

commands.name: agents versions publish
commands.description:
Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it, so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is `rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

flags.name: if-match

flags.description: When publishing 'draft': the name of the new version the draft is kept as.

flags.name: note

commands.summary: Set up the AI coding tools in this project (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI) to work with Caitlyn
commands.description:
AI coding tools work best with Caitlyn when they know how to use the CLI safely. setup finds the tools this project
uses from their files, and gives each what it reads: the Caitlyn CLI section in its instructions file, the CLI's
skill for Claude Code, and the workspace's MCP server. It shows every change before writing anything, writes
only inside the project, and never writes credentials. status says what is set up and whether it is out of date
for this version of the CLI; remove takes it out again, keeping everything else in each file.

stays as it was, and a file left with nothing in it is deleted. A skill edited by hand since setup wrote it is
only removed once you agree. .caitlyn.toml is configuration rather than something setup owns, so it stays:
caitlyn config unset workspace --project removes its workspace.

--tools takes out only what those tools use; AGENTS.md, which Cursor and Codex both read, goes when both are named.
Like setup, it shows the plan and asks first, and under an AI tool it needs --yes.

commands.name: ai setup
commands.summary: Set up this project's AI coding tools to work with Caitlyn
commands.description:
Finds the AI coding tools this project uses (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot in VS Code and Gemini
CLI) from their files in it, shows what it would write for them, and writes only what you accept:

  instructions   The Caitlyn CLI section, in each tool's own file: AGENTS.md (Codex, Cursor), CLAUDE.md (Claude Code,
                 as one @AGENTS.md line when AGENTS.md has the section), .github/copilot-instructions.md, GEMINI.md
  skill          The CLI's skill for Claude Code, .claude/skills/caitlyn/, made from the CLI you have installed
  mcp            The workspace's MCP server, in .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json and .vscode/mcp.json
  defaults       .caitlyn.toml naming this project's workspace (not chosen unless you choose it)

Nothing is written until you agree to the plan; --dry-run only shows it, with every change as a diff in JSON.
Running it again changes nothing that is already right. No credentials go into any file: each tool signs in to
the workspace itself. Every file it writes is marked, so caitlyn ai status reports it and caitlyn ai remove takes it
out again, even in a copy of the repository someone else cloned.

The files name the workspace. For a public repository, --no-workspace leaves it out (and the MCP server and
project defaults with it).

--update regenerates what is already set up, and adds nothing; --check says whether any of it is out of date for
this version of the CLI, and exits 3 if it is, for CI.

An AI tool may run it: it never asks, prints the plan as JSON, and writes only with --yes, once the person has
seen the plan, because these files tell AI tools how to behave. It never changes agent scopes.

commands.name: api
commands.summary: Call any operation by name, or any path, including ones newer than this CLI
commands.description:
For what no other command covers yet: an operation newer than this CLI, or a raw request while you work out
what an integration should send. Prefer the named commands, which check their input and say what they change.

Calls any Caitlyn operation by its name, or any path by method and path (the CLI design, 2.6).

By operation name, the input is checked against the model this CLI was built from: give members as flags
(--knowledge-base-id, or the identifier's short flag such as --kb), with --field key=value, or the whole input
with --input file.json (- for stdin). Retries, idempotency keys, If-Match, the release check and typed errors
all apply.

By method and path, nothing is checked, which reaches an operation newer than the CLI. --field key=value (numbers
and booleans parsed, @file reads a file, json: parses JSON) and --raw-field key=value (always text) build the
query (GET, DELETE) or the JSON body (otherwise). --paginate follows nextCursor.

--include prints the status line and response headers first. --describe prints an operation's input and output
as JSON Schema.

commands.name: apply
commands.summary: Write agents' drafts from a folder of files
commands.description:
The step after diff: apply writes the agents' drafts from the folder of files export made, after you've
reviewed the plan. Use it from your terminal, or from CI once a change to the files is merged; --publish then
makes the drafts live in the same step.

Plans again (the workspace may have moved since you last looked), shows the plan, asks, then replaces each changed
agent's draft, sending the ETag of the draft it planned against, so a draft someone changed meanwhile is refused
(exit 7) rather than overwritten. Unchanged files change nothing, so running it again is safe. Live doesn't change:
publish with caitlyn agents versions publish, or --publish --name here.

--publish publishes every agent whose live version isn't its file, except where someone rolled live back: while
an agent's newest live change is a rollback, --publish leaves it alone whatever the file changes, and the same goes
for a file with the content of a version live has pointed at before and was moved away from since. This includes a
file reverted to an earlier configuration that was already published: it isn't published again on its own. --publish-over-rollback publishes those too, with --confirm naming them in CI and under an AI agent; or
publish one by hand with caitlyn agents versions publish.

flags.description: The note written with the publish

flags.name: publish
flags.description: Publish the drafts afterwards (a separate step: live changes)

commands.name: auth
commands.summary: Sign in, sign out, and see who you're signed in as
commands.description:
Sign in once per workspace with auth login: your browser opens the workspace's sign-in page, and the tokens are
kept in your operating system's keychain under a profile. auth status says who you are signed in as and how;
switch changes which profile is used by default. In CI, sign in with environment variables or the pipeline's
own identity instead of a profile.

commands.name: auth login
commands.description:
Sign in to a Caitlyn workspace and save it as a profile.

By default the CLI opens your browser at the workspace's sign-in page; approve there, after checking that it names
"Caitlyn CLI" and the workspace. On a machine with no browser, --device shows a code to approve from any other
device. --with-token reads a personal access token from stdin instead.

Tokens go to your operating system's keychain, never to the configuration file. Where there is no keychain,
--insecure-storage keeps them in ~/.caitlyn/credentials (readable only by you), and auth status says so every time.

At a terminal, sign-in then asks how the profile shows output, and what an AI agent may do with it. Elsewhere, the
--output-default, --agent-output and --agent-scopes flags answer those questions; without them nothing is saved.

In CI, sign in with the pipeline's own identity instead: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/ci/#signing-in-without-secrets

Sign out of the profile's workspace: the refresh token is revoked at the workspace, and the profile's tokens,
and any AI agent's token made from them, are removed from the keychain (or the credentials file).

The profile's settings stay in ~/.caitlyn/config. A personal access token is removed but not revoked: revoke it in
Caitlyn.

paste it into chats, issues, prompts or logs, and don't save it in a file. AI agents are refused it.

commands.name: chat
commands.summary: Talk to an agent from your terminal, or ask it one question and get its cited answer
commands.description:
The quickest way to try an agent. On a terminal with no message, chat opens a conversation you type into:
each answer streams in with its sources, /attach <file> sends a file with the next message, /new starts a new
conversation and /quit (or Ctrl-D) ends it. Give a message to ask one question and exit, which is what scripts
and CI use, or - to read it from stdin. AGENT@draft talks to the draft, so you can try a change before
publishing it. On a terminal, chat renders the answer whatever output your configuration sets: give
--output jsonl on the command for its events as data.

Starts a conversation with an agent (AGENT alone is its live version) and streams the answer, or continues
one with --conversation. The answer streams to stdout; progress shows on stderr; citations print as numbered
sources at the end. A message of - is read from stdin.

-o jsonl prints every event, for scripts and AI agents. Ctrl-C stops reading: the answer carries on in Caitlyn,
and the CLI prints the command that follows it.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/ask-an-agent/

JSON document for AI agents and scripts: every command's flags with their types, enum values and whether they are
required; its impact class (read, write, user-facing or destructive); whether it is long-running, interactive-only
or beta; the permission and scope it needs; the exit codes it can end with, and the error codes behind them; its

commands.name: conversations send
commands.description:
Sends a message and streams the answer as server-sent events.

The message is sent when the call is made, whether or not anyone reads the stream. The stream ends with exactly one `message.completed` or `message.failed`. If the connection drops, the SDK re-attaches with `WatchConversation` and `Last-Event-ID`, so no event is lost or repeated. Not retried automatically: a send that fails before the stream starts is reported to the caller.

A message may carry documents in `attachments`, each named by an upload reserved for this conversation. The SDKs also take files there: each file is uploaded for the conversation first, and the message is sent once every upload has arrived.

Only a participant may send: whoever started the conversation, or someone it is shared with for writing (the update grant), who may still see the conversation's agent and holds that agent's version access grant (the conversation's version may be `live`). A caller without any of these gets 404, so revoking someone's access to the agent stops them chatting in conversations they already started.

commands.name: conversations watch
commands.description:
Watches a conversation: the answer being written, if any, then every answer after it, until the caller closes the stream. An answer whose stream ended moments before the watch opened may still be delivered, from its `message.started` event; match answers on your own message ID.

Opened without `Last-Event-ID` while an answer is being written, the watch replays that answer from its start, so it shows the answer so far. An answer too long for the replay buffer cannot be replayed: the watch sends `stream.reset` instead, then the answers after it. Read the turn with ListMessages once it ends.

With `Last-Event-ID`, it resumes from the event after that one, so a dropped connection loses nothing; the SDKs use this to re-attach to `SendMessage`, and to reconnect a dropped watch. When the answer that event belongs to has ended, or can no longer be replayed, the watch sends `stream.reset` with a new cursor instead, then carries on. Each answer ends with `message.completed` or `message.failed`, which end that answer but not the stream, so helpers watch for the event they need and then close.

commands.name: core ingestion complete-uploads
commands.description:
Reports that items' bytes are in place, so they can be ingested.

Takes 1 to 100 item identifiers, each awaiting upload. For each, the server checks that the uploaded object's stored SHA-256 and size match the item's, and that the caller may still write to the item's folder, then starts its ingestion. Returns 200 with a result for each item, in request order: `accepted`, or `failed` with `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` (the object is deleted; upload it again), `NOT_FOUND` (nothing was uploaded to the item's key), `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `UPLOAD_EXPIRED` or `CONFLICT` (the item is not awaiting upload). One failed item never stops the others. The SDKs always call this for you. An upload nobody reports is found by the server within about a minute, while the batch has items awaiting upload, and goes through the same checks; only an item whose bytes are still missing when its reservation ends fails, with `UPLOAD_EXPIRED`.

commands.name: core operations cancel
commands.description:
Cancels an Operation's work.

Work not started yet is dropped; work running is stopped. Only `document_ingestion` can be cancelled today: a cancelled first version removes the document, and a cancelled new version leaves the current one serving. Needs the files update permission. A caller without it gets 404, as for an Operation it may not see.

Streams the workspace's events the caller asks for, from a cursor or from now.

A stream listens to what it names and nothing else: give `type`, `conversationId`, or both. Every event is about a subject (a conversation, for now), and the caller receives it only when it may read that subject, decided per event as a read of the subject would be: the same permission and, for a token, the same scope. A cursor the stream cannot carry on from is answered with `stream.reset` and a new cursor, not an error. To wait for something your own call will cause, open the stream first, then make the call.

commands.name: knowledge-bases access get
commands.description:
Gets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

Without `folder` or `document`, the knowledge base's role grants (`roles`). With `folder`, that folder's `readers`; with `document`, that document's. `inheritedFrom` names the folder whose readers apply when they are inherited. A folder or document the caller may not see is 404. The root folder (`folder=/`, `kb.folders('/').access`) holds the readers every folder falls back to; its readers are never inherited.

For a folder or document, the `readers` also come back on ListFolders, ListDocuments and GetDocument too, with `inheritedFrom`, under the files list and read permissions. What GetAccess adds is the access on its own, with the ETag that SetAccess's `If-Match` takes, and the root folder's readers; reading it needs the files permissions list permission.

commands.name: knowledge-bases access set
commands.description:
Sets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it the write is unconditional and the last writer wins, which is safe because the caller sends the whole list. With it, access that changed since is refused with 412.

Without `folder` or `document`, send `roles`: the roles sent become the whole list. With `folder` or `document`, send `readers`; `kind: inherit` makes it follow its folder again. The knowledge base's role grants are set only without a target, under the knowledge base's own permission, as v2's knowledge base permissions route sets them, so `roles` with `folder` or `document`, `readers` without one, and both `folder` and `document` are refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The root folder (`folder=/`) holds the readers every other folder falls back to, so `inherit` is refused there with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Applying readers to the passages a folder or document holds continues after the response; the returned access says what is set, and the knowledge base's watch shows the work.

Setting `roles` is refused in two cases, as in v2. A caller may give a role only a grant it could make itself: any other is refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. And a grant that is not safe for guests, given to a role that guests or anonymous visitors use, is refused with 422 `RBAC_NOT_GUEST_SAFE`. Only the grants being added are judged, so a grant the role already holds never blocks an unrelated change. Both checks are made by the server on the roles sent.

commands.name: knowledge-bases documents versions delete

commands.name: knowledge-bases folders access get
commands.description:
Gets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

Without `folder` or `document`, the knowledge base's role grants (`roles`). With `folder`, that folder's `readers`; with `document`, that document's. `inheritedFrom` names the folder whose readers apply when they are inherited. A folder or document the caller may not see is 404. The root folder (`folder=/`, `kb.folders('/').access`) holds the readers every folder falls back to; its readers are never inherited.

For a folder or document, the `readers` also come back on ListFolders, ListDocuments and GetDocument too, with `inheritedFrom`, under the files list and read permissions. What GetAccess adds is the access on its own, with the ETag that SetAccess's `If-Match` takes, and the root folder's readers; reading it needs the files permissions list permission.

commands.name: knowledge-bases folders access set
commands.description:
Sets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it the write is unconditional and the last writer wins, which is safe because the caller sends the whole list. With it, access that changed since is refused with 412.

Without `folder` or `document`, send `roles`: the roles sent become the whole list. With `folder` or `document`, send `readers`; `kind: inherit` makes it follow its folder again. The knowledge base's role grants are set only without a target, under the knowledge base's own permission, as v2's knowledge base permissions route sets them, so `roles` with `folder` or `document`, `readers` without one, and both `folder` and `document` are refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The root folder (`folder=/`) holds the readers every other folder falls back to, so `inherit` is refused there with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Applying readers to the passages a folder or document holds continues after the response; the returned access says what is set, and the knowledge base's watch shows the work.

Setting `roles` is refused in two cases, as in v2. A caller may give a role only a grant it could make itself: any other is refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. And a grant that is not safe for guests, given to a role that guests or anonymous visitors use, is refused with 422 `RBAC_NOT_GUEST_SAFE`. Only the grants being added are judged, so a grant the role already holds never blocks an unrelated change. Both checks are made by the server on the roles sent.

commands.name: knowledge-bases ingestion batches create
commands.description:
Makes an ingestion batch for one knowledge base, and plans it unless more items will follow.

Takes up to 10,000 items; add more with BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems while `awaitMoreItems` is true. Returns 202 with the batch, and `Location` names it; wait for the plan with the SDKs' `batch.planned()`. Needs the ingestion create permission and read access to the knowledge base, as v2's ingestion route does. A batch that needs bytes uploaded also needs the files create permission to be started with StartIngestionBatch, which hands out the upload policy; a batch that needs none runs without that call under `start: when_planned`. A `fetchUrl` item needs the files create permission when it is added, which the server checks, because the trait cannot follow an item's member.

Each item that removes a document (`remove`, or an overwrite) is checked by the server for the files delete permission, and each item that moves one, or adds a new version of one, for the files update permission, and the token's scope covers it too. An item that fails the check is marked `failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the rest carry on. This holds whether the batch starts through StartIngestionBatch or by itself under `start: when_planned`, so the permission is checked per item, not once on the call.

commands.name: knowledge-bases ingestion batches start
commands.description:
Starts a planned ingestion batch, and returns the upload policy for the items that need bytes.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it, the batch starts as it stands; with it, a batch that changed since that ETag is refused with 412. A stale plan is planned again first. Each item's write is then checked and claimed: a new document is reserved at its path, and an existing one is protected by its own version, so a document that changed since the plan becomes a `changed_since_plan` conflict. An item the caller may not write is marked `failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the rest carry on; the call still answers 202. Refused with 409 `INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED` while any item is `unresolved`. Returns 202 with the batch and one upload policy: list the items to upload with `filter[status][eq]=awaiting_upload`, upload each to its `objectKey`, then report them with CompleteIngestionBatchUploads.

Each item that removes a document (`remove`, or an overwrite) is checked by the server for the files delete permission, and each item that moves one, or adds a new version of one, for the files update permission, and the token's scope covers it too. An item that fails the check is marked `failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the rest carry on. This holds whether the batch starts through StartIngestionBatch or by itself under `start: when_planned`, so the permission is checked per item, not once on the call.

commands.name: knowledge-bases ingestion batches watch
commands.description:
Watches a knowledge base, or one document, folder or batch in it: a snapshot first, then each change.

Every connection starts with `snapshot`: the thing watched as it stands, its running and recently finished jobs, and the progress of each document being processed. Then one event per change. A reconnect needs no cursor, because it starts with a snapshot again; nothing is replayed and nothing is lost. The SDKs build every scope's `watch()` and `wait()` on this: `wait()` returns once no job on the thing is running, or raises the error of the job that failed. Events name a document only to callers who may read it. The server ends the stream after at most an hour, and the SDKs reconnect.

What the caller needs depends on what it watches. The whole knowledge base needs the knowledge base read permission and the files list permission, because the snapshot returns the knowledge base and the documents' progress. One document or folder needs the files list permission. One batch needs the ingestion list permission, because the snapshot returns the batch.

commands.name: login
commands.summary: Sign in to a workspace (the same as auth login)
commands.description:
Sign in to a Caitlyn workspace and save it as a profile.

By default the CLI opens your browser at the workspace's sign-in page; approve there, after checking that it names
"Caitlyn CLI" and the workspace. On a machine with no browser, --device shows a code to approve from any other
device. --with-token reads a personal access token from stdin instead.

Tokens go to your operating system's keychain, never to the configuration file. Where there is no keychain,
--insecure-storage keeps them in ~/.caitlyn/credentials (readable only by you), and auth status says so every time.

At a terminal, sign-in then asks how the profile shows output, and what an AI agent may do with it. Elsewhere, the
--output-default, --agent-output and --agent-scopes flags answer those questions; without them nothing is saved.

In CI, sign in with the pipeline's own identity instead: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/ci/#signing-in-without-secrets

flags.description: The output when an AI agent uses the profile: json, yaml, text or same

flags.name: agent-scopes
flags.description: What an AI agent may do with the profile: read-only, full, none, or scopes separated by commas

flags.name: device
flags.description: Sign in with a code approved on another device (RFC 8628), for a terminal with no browser

flags.name: insecure-storage
flags.description: Keep tokens in ~/.caitlyn/credentials (mode 0600) instead of the keychain

flags.name: output-default
flags.description: The profile's default output: auto, table, json, jsonl, yaml or text

flags.name: read-only
flags.description: Ask for the api:read scope only, and refuse every command that writes with this profile

flags.name: scopes
flags.description: The scopes to ask for; the workspace narrows them to your own permissions

flags.name: with-token
flags.description: Read a personal access token from stdin

commands.name: mcp
commands.summary: Add Caitlyn to Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code as an MCP server, so you can use your workspace's agents and knowledge bases from that tool's chat
commands.description:
Your workspace has an MCP server, at https://<workspace>/api/mcp. mcp add gives an AI client (Claude Code, Cursor
or VS Code) the configuration that connects it there; the client then signs you in itself, and its chat can ask
your agents and search your knowledge bases. The CLI only writes the configuration: it never hands the client
its own token.

commands.name: mcp add
commands.summary: Add Caitlyn as an MCP server to Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code
commands.description:
Connects an AI client to the profile's workspace's MCP server, https://<workspace>/api/mcp, for conversational
work over the workspace from the client itself. The client is one of: claude-code, cursor, vscode.

It prints the configuration, or with --write adds it to the client's file in this project (.mcp.json for Claude
Code, .cursor/mcp.json for Cursor, .vscode/mcp.json for VS Code), keeping every other server there. The client then
signs you in to the workspace with its own OAuth sign-in: the CLI never hands its token to another program.

commands.name: me
commands.summary: Show who you're signed in as, and with which credential
commands.description:
Prints who the current profile's credential acts for: the person or API client, the credential's kind and
scopes, and the organisation. Use it to check a sign-in works, or that a CI job is acting as the client you
expect. auth status says the same with how the credential is kept and when it expires.

Needs:
  Signed in to the workspace; no permission beyond that.

Impact: Reads only.

When it fails:
  401 UNAUTHENTICATED          A credential that has expired or been revoked.  Exit code 4.

Available from Caitlyn 5.149.0.

commands.name: telemetry
commands.summary: Turn usage data for Caitlyn on or off, and see what it would send
commands.description:
Usage data for Caitlyn: the CLI can send Caitlyn usage data, with a random install ID: which commands and flags
run (never their values), how long they take and how they end. It is opt-in, in every release, beta included,
and off in CI: on turns it on, off turns it off again and deletes anything queued, and status shows whether it
is on and why.

These commands are only about usage data for Caitlyn. Your own traces (OpenTelemetry to your own collector) are
separate: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT turns them on.

What is sent: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/telemetry/

commands.name: telemetry flush
commands.summary: Send queued usage data for Caitlyn now (the CLI runs this in the background)
commands.description:
Sends any queued events now. The CLI does this in the background after commands; you'd only run it to check that
the endpoint is reachable.

commands.name: telemetry off
commands.summary: Turn usage data for Caitlyn off and delete anything queued
commands.description:
Turns usage data for Caitlyn off for this machine and deletes anything queued and not yet sent. Your own traces
are unaffected.

commands.name: telemetry on
commands.summary: Turn usage data for Caitlyn on: send usage data from this machine
commands.description:
Turns usage data for Caitlyn on for this machine: it is off until you do. CAITLYN_TELEMETRY=0 and
DO_NOT_TRACK still turn it off, and it stays off in CI unless CAITLYN_TELEMETRY=1.

commands.name: telemetry reset
commands.summary: Make a new random install ID for usage data for Caitlyn, and delete anything queued
commands.description:
Makes a new random install ID for usage data for Caitlyn, so later events can't be linked to earlier ones,
and deletes anything queued.

commands.name: telemetry status
commands.summary: Say whether usage data for Caitlyn is on, and why
commands.description:
Says whether usage data for Caitlyn is on and which rule decided it. --pending prints exactly what is
queued, as it would be sent. Your own traces aren't covered here: they follow OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.

reference:
Every command the CLI has, generated from the CLI itself. Each group has a page, with a section for each of its commands. `caitlyn commands --json` prints the same as data.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn agents`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/) | Create agents and change what they answer with, from their draft to the version people talk to |
| [`caitlyn ai`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/ai/) | Set up the AI coding tools in this project (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI) to work with Caitlyn |
| [`caitlyn api`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/api/) | Call any operation by name, or any path, including ones newer than this CLI |
| [`caitlyn apply`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/apply/) | Write agents' drafts from a folder of files |
| [`caitlyn auth`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/) | Sign in, sign out, and see who you're signed in as |
| [`caitlyn chat`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/chat/) | Talk to an agent from your terminal, or ask it one question and get its cited answer |
| [`caitlyn commands`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/commands/) | List every command as data, with its flags, impact and exit codes, for scripts and AI agents |
| [`caitlyn config`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/) | Read and change the CLI's configuration |
| [`caitlyn conversations`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/) | Read, continue and watch conversations |
| [`caitlyn diff`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/diff/) | Compare a folder of agent files with the workspace, to see what apply would change |
| [`caitlyn docs`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/docs/) | Open a command's page in the docs |
| [`caitlyn events`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/events/) | Follow what happens in your workspace as it happens |
| [`caitlyn export`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/export/) | Write agents' configuration to files, to keep as code |
| [`caitlyn help`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/help/) | Help for any command, as text, JSON or Markdown |
| [`caitlyn knowledge-bases`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/knowledge-bases/) | Knowledge bases and their documents, folders, fields and access |
| [`caitlyn login`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/login/) | Sign in to a workspace (the same as auth login) |
| [`caitlyn mcp`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/mcp/) | Add Caitlyn to Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code as an MCP server, so you can use your workspace's agents and knowledge bases from that tool's chat |
| [`caitlyn me`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/me/) | Show who you're signed in as, and with which credential |
| [`caitlyn telemetry`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/telemetry/) | Turn usage data for Caitlyn on or off, and see what it would send |
| [`caitlyn update`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/update/) | Update the CLI, check for an update, or roll one back |
| [`caitlyn version`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/version/) | Show the CLI's version, and what it detected about where it runs |

The low-level building blocks are under [`caitlyn completion`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/completion/): commands most work never needs.

The low-level building blocks are under [`caitlyn core`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/): commands most work never needs.

## Global flags

Every command takes these.

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ci-format` | plain|off | Plain or off: turn off the CI provider's sections, annotations and summaries (auto in CI). |
| `--color` | string | Always, never or auto. |
| `--confirm` | string | Name the target of the highest-impact commands (AI agents and CI). |
| `--debug` | string | Print each request and response on stderr, credentials redacted; --debug=body adds bodies. Given alone, `requests`. |
| `--dry-run` | string | Print the request and send nothing; --dry-run=curl prints it as curl. Given alone, `request`. |
| `--error-format` | human|json | Human or json: how errors are printed on stderr (default: human for a person at a terminal, JSON for scripts, CI and AI agents). Environment: `CAITLYN_ERROR_FORMAT`. |
| `--fail-on` | conditions | Exit non-zero when these hold: the command's conditions, deprecated, skew, or never. |
| `--jq` | string | A jq expression over the result (no jq binary needed). |
| `--no-color` | bool | No colour (the same as --color never). |
| `--no-input` | bool | Never prompt; anything that would ask exits 3 and names the flag that answers it. Environment: `CAITLYN_NO_INPUT`. |
| `--no-pager` | bool | Don't page long output. |
| `--no-project-file` | bool | Ignore any .caitlyn.toml. |
| `-o`, `--output` | string | Table, json, jsonl, yaml or text (default: table on a terminal, JSON when piped). Environment: `CAITLYN_OUTPUT`. |
| `--outputs-file` | string | Write output values as dotenv (GitLab's artifacts:reports:dotenv). |
| `--profile` | string | The profile to use (default: CAITLYN_PROFILE, then the project file, then default). Environment: `CAITLYN_PROFILE`. |
| `--project-file` | string | Read this project file instead of finding .caitlyn.toml. |
| `--query` | string | A JMESPath expression over the result. |
| `--report` | format=path | Write a report beside the output: junit=, markdown=, json= or annotations=\<path> (repeatable). |
| `--show-secret` | bool | In CI, print a secret: auth token's, or a value the API marks sensitive (none yet). Masked first where the CI system can. |
| `--summary-file` | string | Write the run's Markdown summary to this file. |
| `--workspace` | string | The workspace, for example your-company.caitlyn.ai, instead of the profile's. Environment: `CAITLYN_WORKSPACE`. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | bool | Answer yes: run a destructive or user-facing command without asking. |

pages.title: caitlyn agents
pages.summary: Create agents and change what they answer with, from their draft to the version people talk to
pages.markdown:
Create agents and change what they answer with, from their draft to the version people talk to

```sh
caitlyn agents <command> [flags]
```

An agent answers people's questions from the knowledge bases it is given. Each agent has a draft, which is what
you change, named versions saved from it, and live, the version people talk to. Change the draft
(agents draft), save it as a version and compare it with live (agents versions), then publish it; publishing an
earlier version again rolls back, and agents history records every change to live.

To keep agents as files in a repository, use export, diff and apply instead: they read and write the same
drafts.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

```sh
caitlyn agents list
caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL
caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@v13 --expected-live v12
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn agents conversations`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/conversations/) | An agent's conversations |
| [`caitlyn agents create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/#create) | Create an agent |
| [`caitlyn agents delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/#delete) | Delete an agent |
| [`caitlyn agents draft`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/draft/) | An agent's draft: the version you edit |
| [`caitlyn agents get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/#get) | Get an agent |
| [`caitlyn agents history`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/history/) | Every change to an agent's live version, newest first |
| [`caitlyn agents list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/#list) | List agents |
| [`caitlyn agents live`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/live/) | An agent's live version: what people talk to |
| [`caitlyn agents options`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/options/) | What an agent can be configured with in your workspace |
| [`caitlyn agents update`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/#update) | Update an agent |
| [`caitlyn agents versions`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/) | An agent's saved versions, and publishing one as live |

## conversations

An agent's conversations. See [`caitlyn agents conversations`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/conversations/): `list`.

## create

Create an agent (beta).

```sh
caitlyn agents create [flags]
```

Impact: `write`. Its flags, examples and exit codes: [`caitlyn agents create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/create/).

## delete

Delete an agent (beta).

```sh
caitlyn agents delete <agent> [flags]
```

Impact: `destructive`. Its flags, examples and exit codes: [`caitlyn agents delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/delete/).

## draft

An agent's draft: the version you edit. See [`caitlyn agents draft`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/draft/): `compare`, `conversations`, `diff`, `edit`, `get`, `publish`, `replace`, `reset`, `save`, `update`.

## get

Get an agent (beta).

```sh
caitlyn agents get <agent> [flags]
```

Impact: `read`. Its flags, examples and exit codes: [`caitlyn agents get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/get/).

## history

Every change to an agent's live version, newest first. See [`caitlyn agents history`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/history/): `get`, `list`.

## list

List agents (beta).

```sh
caitlyn agents list [flags]
```

Impact: `read`. Its flags, examples and exit codes: [`caitlyn agents list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/list/).

## live

An agent's live version: what people talk to. See [`caitlyn agents live`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/live/): `compare`, `conversations`, `get`.

## options

What an agent can be configured with in your workspace. See [`caitlyn agents options`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/options/): `guardrails`, `memory-stores`, `models`, `tools`, `voices`.

## update

Update an agent (beta).

```sh
caitlyn agents update <agent> [flags]
```

Impact: `write`. Its flags, examples and exit codes: [`caitlyn agents update`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/update/).

## versions

An agent's saved versions, and publishing one as live. See [`caitlyn agents versions`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/): `compare`, `conversations`, `delete`, `get`, `list`, `publish`.

pages.title: caitlyn agents create
pages.markdown:
Create an agent (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents create [flags]
```

Creates an agent with a draft; it has no live version until the draft is published.

The draft starts with `configuration`, or the default configuration without one; change it with UpdateDraftVersion or ReplaceDraftVersion, then publish it with PublishAgentVersion. Returns the agent, and `Location` names it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `agents.create` (scope `agents:write`) |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.agents.create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/create-agent/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/agents`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/create-agent/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-create.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-create.output.json); `caitlyn help agents create --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<file>` | The file to upload, or `-` for stdin with `--file-name`. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--description` | string | What the agent is for. At most 2000 characters. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--idempotency-key` | string | Reuse this key when re-running the same command (default: a new key per run). |
| `--name` | string, required | The agent's name, 1 to 128 characters. At most 128 characters. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# Create an HR assistant
caitlyn agents create --name 'HR assistant' --description 'Answers Harbour Freight staff'\''s leave and pay questions.' \
    --set 'avatar=json:{"colour":"sage","mark":{"icon":"leaf"}}'

# The same idempotency key with a different request: fails with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, exit code 1
caitlyn agents create --idempotency-key 4d5e6f70-8192-4a3b-8c4d-5e6f708192a3 --name 'Pay assistant'
```

## Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 1 | Failed: any error not listed below, and a batch or sync in which some items failed | `ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED` (400), `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE` (400), `INVALID_CURSOR` (400), `UNKNOWN_FIELD` (400), `UNKNOWN_FILTER` (400), `UNKNOWN_SORT` (400), `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `VERSION_NOT_DELETABLE` (400), `BATCH_ITEM_CONTENT_AMBIGUOUS` (422), `CONTENT_REJECTED` (422), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` (422), `METADATA_FIELD_PASSAGE_SCOPED` (422), `METADATA_FIELD_UNDEFINED` (422), `METADATA_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (422), `METADATA_VALUE_INVALID` (422), `RBAC_NOT_GUEST_SAFE` (422), `INTERNAL` (500), `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 3 | Action needed: a plan has unresolved items, a confirmation was needed with no terminal, or --fail-on found changes | `INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED` (409) |
| 4 | Not signed in, or the credential was refused | `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) |
| 5 | Not allowed | `NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIALS` (403), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403), `PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (403) |
| 7 | Conflict or stale | `ALREADY_EXISTS` (409), `CONFLICT` (409), `DOCUMENT_INGESTION_IN_PROGRESS` (409), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE` (409), `OPERATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE` (409), `TARGET_IN_USE` (409), `VERSIONS_NOT_NUMBERED` (409), `VERSION_IN_HISTORY` (409), `VERSION_IN_USE` (409) |
| 8 | Not supported by this workspace's release |  |
| 10 | Could not reach Caitlyn, or the stream was lost |  |
| 11 | Rate limited after retries | `RATE_LIMITED` (429) |
| 130 | Interrupted (Ctrl-C) |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

pages.title: caitlyn agents delete
pages.markdown:
Delete an agent (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents delete <agent> [flags]
```

Deletes an agent, its draft and every version.

Conversations with the agent are kept. Caitlyn's built-in agents (`native`) are defined by the platform and refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Deleting cannot be undone, and is audited.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes`; AI agents and CI also pass `--confirm <agent>` |
| Needs | `agents.delete` (scope `agents:admin`) and delete on the agent; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.agents(agentId).delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/delete-agent/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`DELETE /api/v3/agents/{agentId}`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/delete-agent/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-delete.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-delete.output.json); `caitlyn help agents delete --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<agent>` | The agent. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# Delete an agent
caitlyn agents delete GHT7YRWXPL

# An agent that does not exist, or that the caller may not see: fails with NOT_FOUND, exit code 6
caitlyn agents delete NOPE0000
```

## Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |

pages.markdown:
Update an agent (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents update <agent> [flags]
```

Changes an agent's name, description or avatar; `If-Match` is required.

pages.title: caitlyn agents draft
pages.summary: An agent's draft: the version you edit
pages.markdown:
An agent's draft: the version you edit

```sh
caitlyn agents draft <command> [flags]
```

The draft is the agent's working copy: every change goes here first, and nobody talking to the agent sees it
until it is published. Read it, change members with update, replace it whole, or edit it in your editor; send
the ETag you read with --if-match so you never overwrite someone else's change. When it's ready, save it as a
named version (save) or publish it straight away (publish). reset throws the draft's changes away.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

```sh
caitlyn agents draft get GHT7YRWXPL
caitlyn agents draft update GHT7YRWXPL --set guidance.instructions="Quote the clause you relied on."
caitlyn agents draft save GHT7YRWXPL --name november-candidate
```

pages.title: caitlyn agents draft edit
pages.summary: Edit an agent's draft in your editor, and save it when you close the editor
pages.markdown:
Edit an agent's draft in your editor, and save it when you close the editor

```sh
caitlyn agents draft edit <agent>
```

Opens the agent's draft in your editor ($VISUAL, $EDITOR, or `editor` in configuration) as YAML. When you save
and close it, the CLI shows what changed and replaces the draft, sending the ETag it read, so a draft someone
changed meanwhile is refused (exit 7) rather than overwritten. Nothing is published: save or publish the draft
when it's ready. For changing one member from a script, use agents draft update --set instead.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |


pages.markdown:

pages.title: caitlyn agents draft publish
pages.markdown:
Publish a version (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents draft publish <agent> [flags]
```

Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it, so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is `rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

| Who can run it | People and API clients |

pages.markdown:
Every change to an agent's live version, newest first

```sh
caitlyn agents history <command> [flags]
```

The live history records each publish and rollback: which version went live, which it replaced, who did it and
their note. Read it to see what people were talking to at a given time, or before rolling back.

```sh
caitlyn agents history list --agent GHT7YRWXPL
```

## get

Get a live history entry (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents history get <entry> [flags]
```

Gets one live history entry, with the configuration live had after the change.

The configuration is that of the entry's `version`, which never changes. Reading the entry (who changed live, when, and to which version) needs agent read; its `configuration` needs what reading that version needs, so a caller without the permission to read versions, or without the agent's version access grant, gets the entry without it. It is also absent when that version was deleted through an older API that does not protect versions named in live history.

| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `agents.read` (scope `agents:read`) and read on the agent; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |

| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/agents/{agentId}/history/{historyEntryId}`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/get-history-entry/) |

pages.summary: An agent's live version: what people talk to
pages.markdown:
An agent's live version: what people talk to

```sh
caitlyn agents live <command> [flags]
```

Live is the version people talk to. Read it, compare it with another version, or start a conversation with it.
Live only changes when a version is published (agents versions publish, or agents draft publish), and agents
history records each change.

```sh
caitlyn agents live get GHT7YRWXPL
caitlyn agents live compare GHT7YRWXPL --with-version november-candidate
```

## compare

Compare versions (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents live compare <agent> [flags]
```

Compares two versions of an agent, member by member.

Returns one change per member that differs, from `version` to `with`, each with its value before and after; `before` is absent for a member `with` added, and `after` for one it removed. Lists are compared by their items' keys, so a path reads `workflow.phases[intake].transitions`. Both versions need the same access as reading them.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `agents.aliases.read` (scope `agents:read`) |

| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-live-compare.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-live-compare.output.json); `caitlyn help agents live compare --format json` prints them too |

pages.title: caitlyn agents versions
pages.summary: An agent's saved versions, and publishing one as live
pages.markdown:
An agent's saved versions, and publishing one as live

```sh
caitlyn agents versions <command> [flags]
```

Versions are named, unchangeable snapshots of an agent's draft. Compare two before publishing, publish one to
make it live, or publish an earlier one again to roll back. --expected-live names the version you expect to
replace, so two people publishing at once can't silently overwrite each other.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

```sh
caitlyn agents versions list --agent GHT7YRWXPL
caitlyn agents versions compare GHT7YRWXPL@v13 --with-version november-candidate
caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@november-candidate --expected-live v13
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn agents versions compare`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/#compare) | Compare versions |
| [`caitlyn agents versions conversations`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/conversations/) | Start a conversation with a saved version |
| [`caitlyn agents versions delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/#delete) | Delete a version |
| [`caitlyn agents versions get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/#get) | Get a version |
| [`caitlyn agents versions list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/#list) | List versions |
| [`caitlyn agents versions publish`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/agents/versions/#publish) | Publish a version |

pages.title: caitlyn agents versions compare
pages.markdown:
Compare versions (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents versions compare <agent[@version]> [flags]
```

Compares two versions of an agent, member by member.

Returns one change per member that differs, from `version` to `with`, each with its value before and after; `before` is absent for a member `with` added, and `after` for one it removed. Lists are compared by their items' keys, so a path reads `workflow.phases[intake].transitions`. Both versions need the same access as reading them.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `agents.aliases.read` (scope `agents:read`) |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.agents(agentId).versions(version).compare`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/compare-agent-versions/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/agents/{agentId}/versions/{version}/compare`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/compare-agent-versions/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-versions-compare.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-versions-compare.output.json); `caitlyn help agents versions compare --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<agent>` | The agent. Written `AGENT` or `AGENT@version`: `AGENT` alone means its live version, `AGENT@draft` its draft. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--with-version` | string, required | The version compared to: 'draft', 'live' or a version name. At most 63 characters. Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# What the draft changes from live
caitlyn agents versions compare GHT7YRWXPL --with-version draft

# A version that does not exist, or that the caller may not see: fails with NOT_FOUND, exit code 6
caitlyn agents versions compare GHT7YRWXPL --with-version v99
```

pages.title: caitlyn agents versions delete
pages.markdown:
Delete a version (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents versions delete <agent[@version]> [flags]
```

Deletes a named version that live does not point at and live history does not name.

Versions serve as the record of what live was, so these are refused: `draft` and `live`, which every agent keeps, with 400 `VERSION_NOT_DELETABLE`; the version live points at, with 409 `VERSION_IN_USE` (point live at another version first); and any version a live history entry names, with 409 `VERSION_IN_HISTORY`. A saved version that was never live can be deleted. Like every change, it is audited.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes` |
| Needs | `agents.aliases.delete` (scope `agents:admin`) and delete on the agent; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.agents(agentId).versions(version).delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/delete-agent-version/) |

pages.title: caitlyn agents versions publish
pages.markdown:
Publish a version (beta)

```sh
caitlyn agents versions publish <agent[@version]> [flags]
```

Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it, so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is `rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `user-facing`: changes what other people get; AI agents and CI pass `--yes`; AI agents and CI also pass `--confirm <agent>` |
| Needs | `agents.aliases.publish` (scope `agents:admin`) and update on the agent; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.agents(agentId).versions(version).publish`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/publish-agent-version/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/agents/{agentId}/versions/{version}/publish`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/publish-agent-version/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-versions-publish.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/agents-versions-publish.output.json); `caitlyn help agents versions publish --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<agent>` | The agent. Written `AGENT` or `AGENT@version`: `AGENT` alone means its live version, `AGENT@draft` its draft. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--expected-live` | string | The version the caller expects live to point at now, or 'none' before the agent's first publish. At most 63 characters. Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--idempotency-key` | string | Reuse this key when re-running the same command (default: a new key per run). |
| `--if-match` | string | Only if the thing still has this ETag (412 otherwise). Without it, the change applies to the thing as it is now. |
| `--name` | string | When publishing 'draft': the name of the new version the draft is kept as. At most 63 characters. Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$`. |
| `--note` | string | Why it was published, recorded in the live history entry, at most 2,000 characters. At most 2000 characters. |

```sh
# Publish the tested draft as a new version
caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@draft --expected-live october-release --name november-release \
    --note 'Quotes the policy clause it relied on.'

# Roll back to an earlier version
caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@october-release --note 'The November wording confused casual staff.'

caitlyn agents versions publish GHT7YRWXPL@october-release --expected-live september-release
```

pages.title: caitlyn ai
pages.summary: Set up the AI coding tools in this project (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI) to work with Caitlyn
pages.markdown:
Set up the AI coding tools in this project (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI) to work with Caitlyn

```sh
caitlyn ai <command> [flags]
```

AI coding tools work best with Caitlyn when they know how to use the CLI safely. setup finds the tools this project
uses from their files, and gives each what it reads: the Caitlyn CLI section in its instructions file, the CLI's
skill for Claude Code, and the workspace's MCP server. It shows every change before writing anything, writes
only inside the project, and never writes credentials. status says what is set up and whether it is out of date
for this version of the CLI; remove takes it out again, keeping everything else in each file.

```sh
caitlyn ai setup
caitlyn ai status
caitlyn ai setup --check
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn ai remove`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/ai/#remove) | Take out what ai setup made, keeping everything else |
| [`caitlyn ai setup`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/ai/#setup) | Set up this project's AI coding tools to work with Caitlyn |
| [`caitlyn ai status`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/ai/#status) | What ai setup made in this project, and whether it is out of date |

## remove

Take out what ai setup made, keeping everything else

```sh
caitlyn ai remove
```

Takes out what caitlyn ai setup made, found by the marks it leaves: its section in each instructions file, its
@AGENTS.md line in CLAUDE.md, the skill, and the caitlyn server in each MCP file. Everything else in those files
stays as it was, and a file left with nothing in it is deleted. A skill edited by hand since setup wrote it is
only removed once you agree. .caitlyn.toml is configuration rather than something setup owns, so it stays:
caitlyn config unset workspace --project removes its workspace.

--tools takes out only what those tools use; AGENTS.md, which Cursor and Codex both read, goes when both are named.
Like setup, it shows the plan and asks first, and under an AI tool it needs --yes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` | string | The project folder (default: the repository the working folder is in). |
| `--tools` | string, repeatable | Only what these tools use, separated by commas: claude-code, cursor, codex, copilot, gemini-cli. |
| `--with` | string, repeatable | Only these, separated by commas: instructions, skill, mcp. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
caitlyn ai remove --dry-run

caitlyn ai remove --tools cursor,codex
```

### Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 3 | Action needed: a plan has unresolved items, a confirmation was needed with no terminal, or --fail-on found changes |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

## setup

Set up this project's AI coding tools to work with Caitlyn

```sh
caitlyn ai setup
```

Finds the AI coding tools this project uses (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot in VS Code and Gemini
CLI) from their files in it, shows what it would write for them, and writes only what you accept:

  instructions   The Caitlyn CLI section, in each tool's own file: AGENTS.md (Codex, Cursor), CLAUDE.md (Claude Code,
                 as one @AGENTS.md line when AGENTS.md has the section), .github/copilot-instructions.md, GEMINI.md
  skill          The CLI's skill for Claude Code, .claude/skills/caitlyn/, made from the CLI you have installed
  mcp            The workspace's MCP server, in .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json and .vscode/mcp.json
  defaults       .caitlyn.toml naming this project's workspace (not chosen unless you choose it)

Nothing is written until you agree to the plan; --dry-run only shows it, with every change as a diff in JSON.
Running it again changes nothing that is already right. No credentials go into any file: each tool signs in to
the workspace itself. Every file it writes is marked, so caitlyn ai status reports it and caitlyn ai remove takes it
out again, even in a copy of the repository someone else cloned.

The files name the workspace. For a public repository, --no-workspace leaves it out (and the MCP server and
project defaults with it).

--update regenerates what is already set up, and adds nothing; --check says whether any of it is out of date for
this version of the CLI, and exits 3 if it is, for CI.

An AI tool may run it: it never asks, prints the plan as JSON, and writes only with --yes, once the person has
seen the plan, because these files tell AI tools how to behave. It never changes agent scopes.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | bool | Say whether what is set up is out of date for this CLI, and exit 3 if it is. |
| `--dir` | string | The project folder (default: the repository the working folder is in). |
| `--no-workspace` | bool | Leave the workspace's name out of the files, for a public repository. |
| `--tools` | string, repeatable | The tools to set up, separated by commas: claude-code, cursor, codex, copilot, gemini-cli (default: the ones this project uses). |
| `--update` | bool | Regenerate what is already set up, and add nothing. |
| `--with` | string, repeatable | What to set up, separated by commas: instructions, skill, mcp, defaults (default: all but defaults). |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
caitlyn ai setup

# Only show the plan, for these tools
caitlyn ai setup --tools claude-code,cursor --with instructions,skill,mcp --dry-run

# In CI: fail when the committed files are out of date
caitlyn ai setup --check
```

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 3 | Action needed: a plan has unresolved items, a confirmation was needed with no terminal, or --fail-on found changes |  |
| 5 | Not allowed |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

pages.title: caitlyn api
pages.summary: Call any operation by name, or any path, including ones newer than this CLI
pages.markdown:
Call any operation by name, or any path, including ones newer than this CLI

```sh
caitlyn api <Operation> [--member value …] | api <METHOD> <path>
```

For what no other command covers yet: an operation newer than this CLI, or a raw request while you work out
what an integration should send. Prefer the named commands, which check their input and say what they change.

Calls any Caitlyn operation by its name, or any path by method and path (the CLI design, 2.6).

By operation name, the input is checked against the model this CLI was built from: give members as flags
(--knowledge-base-id, or the identifier's short flag such as --kb), with --field key=value, or the whole input
with --input file.json (- for stdin). Retries, idempotency keys, If-Match, the release check and typed errors
all apply.

By method and path, nothing is checked, which reaches an operation newer than the CLI. --field key=value (numbers
and booleans parsed, @file reads a file, json: parses JSON) and --raw-field key=value (always text) build the
query (GET, DELETE) or the JSON body (otherwise). --paginate follows nextCursor.

--include prints the status line and response headers first. --describe prints an operation's input and output
as JSON Schema.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<Operation>` | Operation. Required. |
| `<METHOD>` | METHOD. Required. |
| `<path>` | Path. Required. |

## Flags

Only the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
caitlyn api GetKnowledgeBase --kb KB4T7YQ2WL

caitlyn api GET /v3/knowledge-bases/KB4T7YQ2WL/documents --field limit=2
```
