pages.title: caitlyn apply
pages.summary: Write agents' drafts from a folder of files
pages.markdown:
Write agents' drafts from a folder of files

```sh
caitlyn apply [flags]
```

The step after diff: apply writes the agents' drafts from the folder of files export made, after you've
reviewed the plan. Use it from your terminal, or from CI once a change to the files is merged; --publish then
makes the drafts live in the same step.

Plans again (the workspace may have moved since you last looked), shows the plan, asks, then replaces each changed
agent's draft, sending the ETag of the draft it planned against, so a draft someone changed meanwhile is refused
(exit 7) rather than overwritten. Unchanged files change nothing, so running it again is safe. Live doesn't change:
publish with caitlyn agents versions publish, or --publish --name here.

--publish publishes every agent whose live version isn't its file, except where someone rolled live back: while
an agent's newest live change is a rollback, --publish leaves it alone whatever the file changes, and the same goes
for a file with the content of a version live has pointed at before and was moved away from since. This includes a
file reverted to an earlier configuration that was already published: it isn't published again on its own. --publish-over-rollback publishes those too, with --confirm naming them in CI and under an AI agent; or
publish one by hand with caitlyn agents versions publish.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | the scope `agents:write` |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--file` | string | The folder exported with caitlyn export. Default: `caitlyn`. |
| `--name` | string | The new version's name, with --publish. |
| `--note` | string | The note written with the publish. |
| `--publish` | bool | Publish the drafts afterwards (a separate step: live changes). |
| `--publish-over-rollback` | bool | With --publish, also publish an agent whose live version was moved away from the file's content (a rollback). |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
caitlyn apply -f caitlyn/ --yes

# Publish the drafts it wrote, naming each agent it publishes
caitlyn apply -f caitlyn/ --yes --publish --name november-release --confirm GHT7YRWXPL
```

pages.title: caitlyn auth
pages.summary: Sign in, sign out, and see who you're signed in as
pages.markdown:
Sign in, sign out, and see who you're signed in as

```sh
caitlyn auth <command> [flags]
```

Sign in once per workspace with auth login: your browser opens the workspace's sign-in page, and the tokens are
kept in your operating system's keychain under a profile. auth status says who you are signed in as and how;
switch changes which profile is used by default. In CI, sign in with environment variables or the pipeline's
own identity instead of a profile.

```sh
caitlyn auth login --workspace your-company.caitlyn.ai
caitlyn auth status
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn auth login`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/#login) | Sign in to a workspace |
| [`caitlyn auth logout`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/#logout) | Sign out: revoke the refresh token and remove the stored tokens |
| [`caitlyn auth status`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/#status) | Show the workspace, who you're signed in as, and how |
| [`caitlyn auth switch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/#switch) | Make a profile the default |
| [`caitlyn auth token`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/auth/#token) | Print the access token, for one-off use with curl |

## login

Sign in to a workspace

```sh
caitlyn auth login
```

Sign in to a Caitlyn workspace and save it as a profile.

By default the CLI opens your browser at the workspace's sign-in page; approve there, after checking that it names
"Caitlyn CLI" and the workspace. On a machine with no browser, --device shows a code to approve from any other
device. --with-token reads a personal access token from stdin instead.

Tokens go to your operating system's keychain, never to the configuration file. Where there is no keychain,
--insecure-storage keeps them in ~/.caitlyn/credentials (readable only by you), and auth status says so every time.

At a terminal, sign-in then asks how the profile shows output, and what an AI agent may do with it. Elsewhere, the
--output-default, --agent-output and --agent-scopes flags answer those questions; without them nothing is saved.

In CI, sign in with the pipeline's own identity instead: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/ci/#signing-in-without-secrets

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent-output` | string | The output when an AI agent uses the profile: json, yaml, text or same. |
| `--agent-scopes` | string | What an AI agent may do with the profile: read-only, full, none, or scopes separated by commas. |
| `--device` | bool | Sign in with a code approved on another device (RFC 8628), for a terminal with no browser. |
| `--insecure-storage` | bool | Keep tokens in ~/.caitlyn/credentials (mode 0600) instead of the keychain. |
| `--output-default` | string | The profile's default output: auto, table, json, jsonl, yaml or text. |
| `--read-only` | bool | Ask for the api:read scope only, and refuse every command that writes with this profile. |
| `--scopes` | string, repeatable | The scopes to ask for; the workspace narrows them to your own permissions. Default: `[api:admin]`. |
| `--with-token` | bool | Read a personal access token from stdin. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
caitlyn auth login --workspace your-company.caitlyn.ai

caitlyn auth login --profile staging --workspace your-company-staging.caitlyn.ai --read-only

caitlyn auth login --device

caitlyn auth login --with-token < token.txt
```

pages.title: caitlyn chat
pages.summary: Talk to an agent from your terminal, or ask it one question and get its cited answer
pages.markdown:
Talk to an agent from your terminal, or ask it one question and get its cited answer

```sh
caitlyn chat [agent[@version]] [message]
```

The quickest way to try an agent. On a terminal with no message, chat opens a conversation you type into:
each answer streams in with its sources, /attach \<file> sends a file with the next message, /new starts a new
conversation and /quit (or Ctrl-D) ends it. Give a message to ask one question and exit, which is what scripts
and CI use, or - to read it from stdin. AGENT@draft talks to the draft, so you can try a change before
publishing it. On a terminal, chat renders the answer whatever output your configuration sets: give
--output jsonl on the command for its events as data.

Starts a conversation with an agent (AGENT alone is its live version) and streams the answer, or continues
one with --conversation. The answer streams to stdout; progress shows on stderr; citations print as numbered
sources at the end. A message of - is read from stdin.

-o jsonl prints every event, for scripts and AI agents. Ctrl-C stops reading: the answer carries on in Caitlyn,
and the CLI prints the command that follows it.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/ask-an-agent/

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | the scope `chat:write` |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<agent[@version]>` | Agent[@version]. Optional. |
| `<message>` | Message. Optional. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--attach` | string, repeatable | Attach a file to the message (repeatable). |
| `--context-file` | string | Structured context for the message: a JSON list of {type, label, uri, data} (at most 20 items, 16 KB). |
| `--conversation` | string | Continue this conversation. |
| `--show` | string, repeatable | Also show: tools, quotes. |
| `--title` | string | A title for a new conversation. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# A conversation, on a terminal
caitlyn chat GHT7YRWXPL

# One question to the draft, and its cited answer
caitlyn chat GHT7YRWXPL@draft "Can I carry leave over to next year?"

# From a script: every event as JSON Lines
caitlyn chat GHT7YRWXPL "Who approves leave?" --output jsonl
```

List every command as data, with its flags, impact and exit codes, for scripts and AI agents

```sh
caitlyn commands
```

Prints the whole command tree of this CLI, hand-written commands included.

On a terminal it is a tree. With --output json (or --json, and whenever the output is not a terminal) it is one
JSON document for AI agents and scripts: every command's flags with their types, enum values and whether they are
required; its impact class (read, write, user-facing or destructive); whether it is long-running, interactive-only
or beta; the permission and scope it needs; the exit codes it can end with, and the error codes behind them; its
examples as command lines; and its page in the docs. It also has the exit-code table, the global flags, whether
the CLI is in agent mode, and the MCP servers that suit some work better than the CLI (alternatives.mcp).

It describes the CLI that is installed, so it always matches the version that runs.

pages.title: caitlyn config
pages.summary: Read and change the CLI's configuration
pages.markdown:
Read and change the CLI's configuration

```sh
caitlyn config <command> [flags]
```

Settings come from, highest first: flags, CAITLYN_ environment variables, the project file .caitlyn.toml, your
user file ~/.caitlyn/config (the selected profile, then its top level), and the built-in defaults. get shows a
setting's effective value and where it came from; set and unset change your user file, a profile, or the project
file; path lists the files read.

```sh
caitlyn config get output --show-origin
caitlyn config set knowledge_base KB4T7YQ2WL --project
caitlyn config list
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn config edit`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#edit) | Edit your configuration file in your editor, and check it when you save |
| [`caitlyn config get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#get) | Show a setting's value, and where it comes from |
| [`caitlyn config list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#list) | List every setting, its value and where it comes from |
| [`caitlyn config path`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#path) | List the configuration files the CLI reads, in order, and whether each exists |
| [`caitlyn config profiles`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#profiles) | List the profiles in your user file, and which is the default |
| [`caitlyn config set`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#set) | Write a setting to your user file, a profile (--profile) or the project file (--project) |
| [`caitlyn config unset`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/config/#unset) | Remove a setting from your user file, a profile (--profile) or the project file (--project) |

Edit your configuration file in your editor, and check it when you save

```sh
caitlyn config edit
```

Opens your user file (or the project file with --project) in your editor, and when you close it checks that the
file loads: an unknown setting or a value of the wrong type is reported, with its line, and you can edit again.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |

pages.title: caitlyn conversations
pages.markdown:
Read, continue and watch conversations

```sh
caitlyn conversations <command> [flags]
```

A conversation is a series of messages with one agent version. Read it, send another message, or watch its
events as they happen. To ask an agent something from your terminal, chat is simpler: it starts or continues a
conversation and streams the answer with its sources.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/ask-an-agent/

```sh
caitlyn conversations get 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1a6b5d8e0f3c
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn conversations get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/#get) | Get a conversation |
| [`caitlyn conversations messages`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/messages/) | A conversation's messages |
| [`caitlyn conversations send`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/#send) | Send a message |
| [`caitlyn conversations watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/#watch) | Watch a conversation |

## get

Get a conversation (beta)

```sh
caitlyn conversations get <conversation> [flags]
```

Gets a conversation: its agent and version, its title and whether it is answering.

Read its messages with ListMessages, and follow it with WatchConversation. A conversation the caller may not see is 404, as one that does not exist is.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `chat-sessions.read` (scope `chat:read`) and read on the conversation; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People, API clients and guests |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.conversations(conversationId).get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/get-conversation/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/conversations/{conversationId}`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/get-conversation/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/conversations-get.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/conversations-get.output.json); `caitlyn help conversations get --format json` prints them too |

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<conversation>` | The conversation. Required. |

### Flags

Only the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# A conversation that is answering
caitlyn conversations get 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47

# A conversation that does not exist, or that the caller may not see: fails with NOT_FOUND, exit code 6
caitlyn conversations get 0193a6f2-0000-7000-8000-000000000000
```

### Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 1 | Failed: any error not listed below, and a batch or sync in which some items failed | `ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED` (400), `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE` (400), `INVALID_CURSOR` (400), `UNKNOWN_FIELD` (400), `UNKNOWN_FILTER` (400), `UNKNOWN_SORT` (400), `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `VERSION_NOT_DELETABLE` (400), `INTERNAL` (500), `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 4 | Not signed in, or the credential was refused | `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) |
| 5 | Not allowed | `NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIALS` (403), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403), `PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (403) |
| 6 | Not found | `NOT_FOUND` (404) |
| 8 | Not supported by this workspace's release |  |
| 10 | Could not reach Caitlyn, or the stream was lost |  |
| 11 | Rate limited after retries | `RATE_LIMITED` (429) |
| 130 | Interrupted (Ctrl-C) |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

## messages

A conversation's messages. See [`caitlyn conversations messages`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/messages/): `list`.

## send

Send a message (beta)

```sh
caitlyn conversations send <conversation> [flags]
```

Sends a message and streams the answer as server-sent events.

The message is sent when the call is made, whether or not anyone reads the stream. The stream ends with exactly one `message.completed` or `message.failed`. If the connection drops, the SDK re-attaches with `WatchConversation` and `Last-Event-ID`, so no event is lost or repeated. Not retried automatically: a send that fails before the stream starts is reported to the caller.

A message may carry documents in `attachments`, each named by an upload reserved for this conversation. The SDKs also take files there: each file is uploaded for the conversation first, and the message is sent once every upload has arrived.

Only a participant may send: whoever started the conversation, or someone it is shared with for writing (the update grant), who may still see the conversation's agent and holds that agent's version access grant (the conversation's version may be `live`). A caller without any of these gets 404, so revoking someone's access to the agent stops them chatting in conversations they already started.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `chats.create` (scope `chat:write`) and update on the conversation; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People, API clients and guests |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Output | A stream of events: one JSON object per event with `--output jsonl` |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.conversations(conversationId).send`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/send-message/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/conversations/{conversationId}/messages`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/send-message/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/conversations-send.input.json); `caitlyn help conversations send --format json` prints them too |

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<conversation>` | The conversation. Required. |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--message` | string, required | The message, at most 32,000 characters. At most 32000 characters. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |
| `--timeout` | string | Stop after this long, for example 10m (exit 9). |
| `--until-match` | string | Exit 0 at the first event this jq expression matches. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# Ask a question
caitlyn conversations send 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47 --message 'How much annual leave do part-time staff get?'

# Ask about an attached document
caitlyn conversations send 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47 --message 'Does this leave form match our policy?' \
    --set 'attachments=json:[{"uploadId":"0193a6f2-1112-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293"}]'

# An attachment whose upload cannot be used: fails with VALIDATION_FAILED, exit code 1
caitlyn conversations send 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47 --message 'Summarise these.' --set 'attachments=json:[{"uploadId":"0193a6f2-1112-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293"},{"uploadId":"0193a6f2-1113-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293"}]'

# A conversation that does not exist, or that the caller may not see: fails with NOT_FOUND, exit code 6
caitlyn conversations send 0193a6f2-0000-7000-8000-000000000000 --message Hello

# An answer is already being written: fails with CONFLICT, exit code 7
caitlyn conversations send 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47 --message 'And for casual staff?'
```

### Exit codes

| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 1 | Failed: any error not listed below, and a batch or sync in which some items failed | `ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED` (400), `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE` (400), `INVALID_CURSOR` (400), `UNKNOWN_FIELD` (400), `UNKNOWN_FILTER` (400), `UNKNOWN_SORT` (400), `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `VERSION_NOT_DELETABLE` (400), `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413), `INTERNAL` (500), `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 3 | Action needed: a plan has unresolved items, a confirmation was needed with no terminal, or --fail-on found changes | `INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED` (409) |
| 4 | Not signed in, or the credential was refused | `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) |
| 5 | Not allowed | `NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIALS` (403), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403), `PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (403) |
| 6 | Not found | `NOT_FOUND` (404) |
| 7 | Conflict or stale | `ALREADY_EXISTS` (409), `CONFLICT` (409), `DOCUMENT_INGESTION_IN_PROGRESS` (409), `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE` (409), `OPERATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE` (409), `TARGET_IN_USE` (409), `VERSIONS_NOT_NUMBERED` (409), `VERSION_IN_HISTORY` (409), `VERSION_IN_USE` (409) |
| 8 | Not supported by this workspace's release |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

## watch

Watch a conversation (beta)

```sh
caitlyn conversations watch <conversation> [flags]
```

Watches a conversation: the answer being written, if any, then every answer after it, until the caller closes the stream. An answer whose stream ended moments before the watch opened may still be delivered, from its `message.started` event; match answers on your own message ID.

Opened without `Last-Event-ID` while an answer is being written, the watch replays that answer from its start, so it shows the answer so far. An answer too long for the replay buffer cannot be replayed: the watch sends `stream.reset` instead, then the answers after it. Read the turn with ListMessages once it ends.

With `Last-Event-ID`, it resumes from the event after that one, so a dropped connection loses nothing; the SDKs use this to re-attach to `SendMessage`, and to reconnect a dropped watch. When the answer that event belongs to has ended, or can no longer be replayed, the watch sends `stream.reset` with a new cursor instead, then carries on. Each answer ends with `message.completed` or `message.failed`, which end that answer but not the stream, so helpers watch for the event they need and then close.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `chat-session-messages.read` (scope `chat:read`) |
| Who can run it | People, API clients and guests |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Output | A stream of events: one JSON object per event with `--output jsonl` |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.conversations(conversationId).watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/watch-conversation/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/conversations/{conversationId}/stream`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/watch-conversation/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/conversations-watch.input.json); `caitlyn help conversations watch --format json` prints them too |

| --- | --- |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--last-event-id` | string | The 'id' of the last event received. At most 128 characters. |
| `--timeout` | string | Stop after this long, for example 10m (exit 9). |
| `--until-match` | string | Exit 0 at the first event this jq expression matches. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
caitlyn conversations watch 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47 --last-event-id 8f14e45f-ceea-4c6b-9d2a-1b3c5d7e9f20.42
```

pages.title: caitlyn conversations messages
pages.markdown:
A conversation's messages

```sh
caitlyn conversations messages <command> [flags]
```

Lists a conversation's messages, oldest first, with their citations.

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn conversations messages list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/conversations/messages/#list) | List messages |

## list

List messages (beta)

```sh
caitlyn conversations messages list [flags]
```

Lists a conversation's messages, oldest first: the caller's and the agent's.

An answer still being written is not listed until it ends; follow it with WatchConversation.

| | |

## content

Link to a document's bytes (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core documents content [flags]
```

Redirects to a short-lived address for a document's bytes, for links and command-line tools.

Answers 302, with `Location` the address, which works for 15 minutes and needs no credential, so treat it as a secret. Without `version`, the current version's bytes. Use it as a link's target, or with `curl -L`. A browser script cannot read a redirect's address: it calls GetDocumentDownload, which answers with the address as JSON, as the SDKs' `doc.download()` does.

## add-items

Add items to a batch (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core ingestion add-items [flags]
```

Adds up to 10,000 more items to a batch that is still `draft`, with a result for each.

A batch takes at most 100,000 items, at most 1,000 of them with `fetchUrl`. The call returns 200 even when every item fails: `results` has one entry per item, in request order, each `created` with the item, or `failed` with a problem (for example 422 `BATCH_ITEM_CONTENT_AMBIGUOUS`). One bad item never refuses the rest. A batch that is not `draft` is refused with 409 `CONFLICT`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.ingestions.create` (scope `knowledge-bases:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.core.ingestion.addItems`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/batch-create-ingestion-batch-items/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/ingestion-batches/{ingestionBatchId}/items:batch-create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/batch-create-ingestion-batch-items/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-ingestion-add-items.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-ingestion-add-items.output.json); `caitlyn help core ingestion add-items --format json` prints them too |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--batch` | string | The ingestion batch. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--knowledge-base`, `--kb` | string | The knowledge base (default: knowledge_base from configuration). Environment: `CAITLYN_KNOWLEDGE_BASE`. |
| `--last` | boolean | True when these are the last items: the batch then stops taking items and is planned. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# Add two items, one of which describes its content twice
caitlyn core ingestion add-items --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --batch 0193a6f3-0001-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 --set 'items=json:[{"path":"/hr/pay-policy.pdf","sha256":"n4bQgYhMfWWaL+qgxVrQFaO/TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg=","byteSize":482113,"contentType":"application/pdf"},{"path":"/hr/code-of-conduct.pdf","sha256":"n4bQgYhMfWWaL+qgxVrQFaO/TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg=","byteSize":482113,"contentType":"application/pdf","fetchUrl":"https://intranet.harbourfreight.example/conduct.pdf"}]'

# A batch that has stopped taking items: fails with CONFLICT, exit code 7
caitlyn core ingestion add-items --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --batch 0193a6f3-0001-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 --set 'items=json:[]'
```

## complete-uploads

Report finished uploads (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core ingestion complete-uploads [flags]
```

Reports that items' bytes are in place, so they can be ingested.

Takes 1 to 100 item identifiers, each awaiting upload. For each, the server checks that the uploaded object's stored SHA-256 and size match the item's, and that the caller may still write to the item's folder, then starts its ingestion. Returns 200 with a result for each item, in request order: `accepted`, or `failed` with `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` (the object is deleted; upload it again), `NOT_FOUND` (nothing was uploaded to the item's key), `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `UPLOAD_EXPIRED` or `CONFLICT` (the item is not awaiting upload). One failed item never stops the others. The SDKs always call this for you. An upload nobody reports is found by the server within about a minute, while the batch has items awaiting upload, and goes through the same checks; only an item whose bytes are still missing when its reservation ends fails, with `UPLOAD_EXPIRED`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.ingestions.create` (scope `knowledge-bases:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.core.ingestion.completeUploads`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/complete-ingestion-batch-uploads/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/ingestion-batches/{ingestionBatchId}/complete-uploads`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/complete-ingestion-batch-uploads/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-ingestion-complete-uploads.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-ingestion-complete-uploads.output.json); `caitlyn help core ingestion complete-uploads --format json` prints them too |

| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--item-ids` | list of string, repeatable, required | The items whose bytes are in place: 1 to 100, each at most once. (required) Repeat the flag, or separate values with commas. |
| `--knowledge-base`, `--kb` | string | The knowledge base (default: knowledge_base from configuration). Environment: `CAITLYN_KNOWLEDGE_BASE`. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

```sh

caitlyn core ingestion complete-uploads --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --batch 0193a6f3-0001-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 \
    --item-ids item-0001 --item-ids item-0002

caitlyn core ingestion complete-uploads --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --batch 0193a6f3-0000-7000-8000-000000000000 \
    --item-ids item-0001
```

## upload-policy

Get the upload policy (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core ingestion upload-policy [flags]
```

Renews a running batch's upload policy before it expires.

pages.markdown:
Work with operations

```sh
caitlyn core operations <command> [flags]
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn core operations cancel`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/operations/#cancel) | Cancel an operation |
| [`caitlyn core operations get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/operations/#get) | Get an operation |
| [`caitlyn core operations list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/operations/#list) | List operations |
| [`caitlyn core operations watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/operations/#watch) | Watch an operation |

## cancel

Cancel an operation (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core operations cancel <operation> [flags]
```

Cancels an Operation's work.

Work not started yet is dropped; work running is stopped. Only `document_ingestion` can be cancelled today: a cancelled first version removes the document, and a cancelled new version leaves the current one serving. Any other kind is refused with 409 `OPERATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE`, and a final Operation with 409 `CONFLICT`. Returns the Operation, which becomes `cancelled` once the work has stopped.

Needs the files update permission. For `document_ingestion` the server also checks, on the document the Operation reads, the permission that started it (`files.create` for a new document, `files.update` for a new version or a retry) and the document's readers. A caller without it gets 404, as for an Operation it may not see.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes` |
| Needs | `files.update` (scope `files:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.core.operations(knowledgeBaseId, operationId).cancel`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/cancel-operation/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/operations/{operationId}/cancel`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/cancel-operation/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-operations-cancel.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-operations-cancel.output.json); `caitlyn help core operations cancel --format json` prints them too |

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<operation>` | The operation. Required. |

### Flags

pages.markdown:
Work with uploads

```sh

```

| Command | Description |

| [`caitlyn core uploads get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/core/uploads/#get) | Get an upload |

## get

Get an upload (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core uploads get <upload> [flags]
```

Gets an upload's status and when its upload URL expires.

Use it to check that the bytes arrived before passing the upload's `id` to the operation that uses it. Only the person or client that reserved the upload can read it; anyone else gets 404.

| | |

| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `files.create` (scope `files:write`) and owner on the upload; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |

| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |

| `<upload>` | The upload. Required. |

### Flags

Only the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh

caitlyn core uploads get 0193a6f2-1111-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293

# An upload that does not exist, or that someone else reserved: fails with NOT_FOUND, exit code 6
```

## reserve

Reserve an upload (beta)

```sh
caitlyn core uploads reserve [flags]
```

Reserves a short-lived slot for a file's bytes and returns a presigned URL bound to their checksum.

Send the bytes with `uploadMethod` to `uploadUrl`, with every header in `requiredHeaders`, before `expiresAt`; then pass the upload's `id` to the operation that uses it. Files can be at most 2 GB. For an attachment, name the conversation in `purpose`: the conversation's attachment settings are checked here, before the bytes travel. The SDKs' `core.uploads.send(file)` does all of this, and their document and attachment helpers call it for you. Many files at once go through an ingestion batch instead, which signs one upload policy for them all.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `files.create` (scope `files:write`) |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.core.uploads.reserve`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/create-upload/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/uploads`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/create-upload/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-uploads-reserve.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/core-uploads-reserve.output.json); `caitlyn help core uploads reserve --format json` prints them too |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--byte-size` | integer, required | The file's size in bytes, at most 2 GB (2,147,483,648 bytes). From 1 to any. |
| `--content-type` | string, required | The file's media type. At most 255 characters. |
| `--expires-in-seconds` | integer | How long the upload URL works: from a minute to an hour, and 15 minutes when absent. From 60 to 3600. Default: `900`. |
| `--file-name` | string, required | The file's name on the caller's machine. At most 1024 characters. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--idempotency-key` | string | Reuse this key when re-running the same command (default: a new key per run). |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |
| `--sha256` | string, required | The base64-encoded SHA-256 of the file's bytes. At most 44 characters. Matches `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=$`. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# Reserve an upload for a PDF
caitlyn core uploads reserve --file-name leave-policy.pdf --content-type application/pdf --byte-size 482113 \
    --sha256 n4bQgYhMfWWaL+qgxVrQFaO/TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg=

# A file over the size limit: fails with PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, exit code 1
caitlyn core uploads reserve --file-name archive.zip --content-type application/zip --byte-size 9000000000 \
    --sha256 n4bQgYhMfWWaL+qgxVrQFaO/TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg=

# An attachment for a conversation whose agent takes none: fails with ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED, exit code 1
caitlyn core uploads reserve --file-name q3.pdf --content-type application/pdf --byte-size 482113 \
    --sha256 n4bQgYhMfWWaL+qgxVrQFaO/TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg= --set 'purpose=json:{"conversationId":"0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47"}'
```

| 4 | Not signed in, or the credential was refused | `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) |

pages.title: caitlyn diff
pages.summary: Compare a folder of agent files with the workspace, to see what apply would change
pages.markdown:
Compare a folder of agent files with the workspace, to see what apply would change

```sh
caitlyn diff [flags]
```

The first step before changing agents from files: diff reads the folder export wrote (caitlyn.yaml and one
file per agent), compares each file with the agent's current draft, and shows what apply would change, member
by member. Nothing is changed. In a merge request, run it with --fail-on changes, --report markdown=plan.md to
post the plan, or --report junit=plan.xml for the test report; then apply writes the drafts once the change is
merged.

It also shows an agent whose draft matches its file but whose live version doesn't: a draft written but not
yet published, which apply --publish would publish.

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/change-an-agent-safely/

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | the scope `agents:read` |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-f`, `--file` | string | The folder exported with caitlyn export. Default: `caitlyn`. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# Plan the folder export wrote
caitlyn diff -f caitlyn/

# In CI: fail when anything would change, and keep the plan as Markdown
caitlyn diff -f caitlyn/ --fail-on changes --report markdown=plan.md
```

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |

| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |

pages.title: caitlyn events
pages.summary: Follow what happens in your workspace as it happens
pages.markdown:
Follow what happens in your workspace as it happens

```sh
caitlyn events <command> [flags]
```

Workspace events report changes as they happen: documents processed, conversations started, versions published.
tail follows them from a terminal or a script, filters by type, keeps a checkpoint so a restart resumes where it
left off, and can stop at the first event that matches.

```sh
caitlyn events tail --type document.processed
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn events tail`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/events/#tail) | Follow workspace events, with checkpoints and match-then-exit |
| [`caitlyn events watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/events/#watch) | Watch the workspace |

## tail

Follow workspace events, with checkpoints and match-then-exit

```sh
caitlyn events tail
```

For scripts that react to the workspace (reprocess a document when it fails, notify a channel when a version is
published) and for watching what happens while you work.

Follows the workspace's events. The stream needs a filter, --type or a subject such as --conversation: there is
no stream of everything.

--checkpoint FILE reads the cursor to start after from the file, and writes each event's id back once the event has
been written to stdout, so a restart misses nothing (delivery is at least once: de-duplicate on id). When the server
can't carry on from a cursor, it sends stream.reset: the CLI prints it (it's data), warns, moves the checkpoint on,
and carries on; --fail-on reset exits 3 instead.

--until-match takes a jq expression and exits 0 at the first event it matches; --timeout bounds the wait. The CLI
prints "Listening." on stderr once the server is listening, so starting the action after it is race-free.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--after` | string | Start after this event id. |
| `--agent` | string, repeatable | Agents to receive events about (repeatable), where the workspace's release supports it. |
| `--checkpoint` | string | Read the start cursor from this file, and write each event's id back after it is printed. |
| `--conversation` | string, repeatable | Conversations to receive events about (repeatable). |
| `--timeout` | duration | Stop after this long (exit 9), for example 10m. Default: `0s`. |
| `--type` | string, repeatable | Event types to receive (repeatable). |
| `--until-match` | string | Exit 0 at the first event this jq expression matches. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
caitlyn events tail --type conversation.created

# Wait for one event, then exit
caitlyn events tail --type document.processed --until-match '.data.documentId == "doc-0003"' --timeout 5m
```

### Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

## watch

Watch the workspace (beta)

```sh
caitlyn events watch [flags]
```

Streams the workspace's events the caller asks for, from a cursor or from now.

A stream listens to what it names and nothing else: give `type`, `conversationId`, or both. Every event is about a subject (a conversation, for now), and the caller receives it only when it may read that subject, decided per event as a read of the subject would be: the same permission and, for a token, the same scope. An answer, a tool call or an input request needs what `WatchConversation` needs; a token whose scopes leave out conversation transcripts receives none of them.

Each event's `id` is a cursor. Send it back as `after` (or `Last-Event-ID` on a reconnect) to carry on from it without missing or repeating an event; without either, the stream starts now. A cursor the stream cannot carry on from is answered with `stream.reset` and a new cursor, not an error. To wait for something your own call will cause, open the stream first, then make the call.

Catching up after a cursor covers activity through the v3 API. A conversation event comes with its content, in the same structures as the conversation's own stream.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Output | A stream of events: one JSON object per event with `--output jsonl` |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.events.watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/watch-workspace-events/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/events/stream`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/watch-workspace-events/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/events-watch.input.json); `caitlyn help events watch --format json` prints them too |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--after` | string | Carry on after this event. At most 128 characters. |
| `--conversation-ids` | list of string, repeatable | The conversations to receive events about. Repeat the flag, or separate values with commas. |
| `--last-event-id` | string | The 'id' of the last event received, sent by a reconnecting client in place of 'after'. At most 128 characters. |
| `--timeout` | string | Stop after this long, for example 10m (exit 9). |
| `--types` | list of string, repeatable | The event types to receive. Repeat the flag, or separate values with commas. |
| `--until-match` | string | Exit 0 at the first event this jq expression matches. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# Wait for any answer in one conversation
caitlyn events watch --types message.completed --types message.failed --conversation-ids 0193a6f2-7c4e-7b1a-9d2e-3f5a8c1b0e47

# Carry on after the last event received
caitlyn events watch --types conversation.created --after 0193a6f3-0a1b-7c2d-8e3f-405162738495

# A stream that names nothing to listen to: fails with VALIDATION_FAILED, exit code 1
caitlyn events watch
```

### Exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Succeeded |  |
| 1 | Failed: any error not listed below, and a batch or sync in which some items failed | `ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED` (400), `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE` (400), `INVALID_CURSOR` (400), `UNKNOWN_FIELD` (400), `UNKNOWN_FILTER` (400), `UNKNOWN_SORT` (400), `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), `VERSION_NOT_DELETABLE` (400), `INTERNAL` (500), `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503) |
| 2 | Usage error: bad flags or arguments, nothing sent |  |
| 4 | Not signed in, or the credential was refused | `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) |
| 5 | Not allowed | `NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIALS` (403), `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403), `PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` (403) |
| 8 | Not supported by this workspace's release |  |
| 9 | Timed out |  |
| 10 | Could not reach Caitlyn, or the stream was lost |  |
| 11 | Rate limited after retries | `RATE_LIMITED` (429) |
| 130 | Interrupted (Ctrl-C) |  |

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

pages.title: caitlyn help
pages.summary: Help for any command, as text, JSON or Markdown
pages.markdown:
Help for any command, as text, JSON or Markdown

```sh
caitlyn help [command]...
```

Help for any command: caitlyn help agents draft save. help also works after a command, as a subcommand:
caitlyn agents help and caitlyn agents draft help show the same as --help there, and so does a command that
takes no argument (caitlyn me help). Where a command takes an argument, help is that argument, so use --help.

Help is text, even when JSON is your configured output; --output json on the command line prints it as data.

--format json prints it as data, with the input's JSON Schema; --format markdown prints the same Markdown as the
command's page in the docs.

Two topics are not commands:
  caitlyn help agents       The AGENTS.md section for AI coding agents (--format markdown), or a Claude Code
                            skill generated from this CLI (--format skill). --write writes it into this project
                            and shows the change; with --dry-run it only shows it. caitlyn ai setup does this for
                            every AI coding tool in the project. For the agents commands: caitlyn agents help, or
                            caitlyn help agents \<command>.
  caitlyn help exit-codes   What every exit code means.

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases
pages.summary: Knowledge bases and their documents, folders, fields and access
pages.markdown:
Knowledge bases and their documents, folders, fields and access

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases <command> [flags]
```

Also: `caitlyn kb`.

A knowledge base holds the documents agents answer from. Add documents one at a time (documents create), or
keep a whole folder in step with one on disk (sync), which only uploads what changed. Documents are processed
before they can be searched: wait, and each document's status, say when that has finished. Folders organise
documents and carry who may read them (access); fields hold structured details about each document.

Recipes: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/look-after-a-knowledge-base/ and https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/keep-a-folder-in-step/

```sh
caitlyn kb list
caitlyn kb documents list --kb KB4T7YQ2WL
caitlyn kb sync KB4T7YQ2WL ./handbook --folder /handbook/
```

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases create
pages.markdown:
Create a knowledge base (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases create [flags]
```

Creates a knowledge base; setting it up continues after the response.

Returns 202 with the knowledge base in `creating`, and `Location` names it; documents can be added once it is `ready`. Where its documents are stored is decided by Caitlyn and never exposed.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.create` (scope `knowledge-bases:write`) |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Long-running | Waits with `--wait` (where it starts work) and `--timeout`; AI agents get a 4-minute default and a command that resumes the wait |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases.create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/create-knowledge-base/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/create-knowledge-base/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-create.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-create.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases create --format json` prints them too |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent-description` | string | What the knowledge base holds, in the words an agent reads to decide when to search it. At most 2000 characters. |
| `--description` | string | What the knowledge base holds, in words for the people who use it. At most 2000 characters. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--idempotency-key` | string | Reuse this key when re-running the same command (default: a new key per run). |

| `--timeout` | string | The wait's time limit, for example 30m (exit 9 when it passes). |
| `--wait` | bool | Wait until the work it starts has finished, then print the thing. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples

```sh
# Create a knowledge base for HR policies
caitlyn knowledge-bases create --name 'HR policies' --description 'Harbour Freight'\''s HR policies, for staff.' \
    --agent-description 'Leave, pay, conduct and safety policies for Harbour Freight staff in New Zealand.'

caitlyn knowledge-bases create --name 'HR policies'
```

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases delete
pages.markdown:
Delete a knowledge base (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases delete <kb> [flags]
```

Deletes a knowledge base and every document in it; the work continues after the response.

Returns 202 with the Operation that tracks it. The knowledge base reads as `deleting` until it is gone, then 404. Deleting cannot be undone.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes`; AI agents and CI also pass `--confirm <kb>` |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.delete` (scope `knowledge-bases:admin`) and delete on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Long-running | Waits with `--wait` (where it starts work) and `--timeout`; AI agents get a 4-minute default and a command that resumes the wait |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).delete`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/delete-knowledge-base/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`DELETE /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/delete-knowledge-base/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-delete.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-delete.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases delete --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<kb>` | The knowledge base. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--progress` | bool | Print progress lines even without a terminal. |
| `--timeout` | string | The wait's time limit, for example 30m (exit 9 when it passes). |
| `--wait` | bool | Wait until the work it starts has finished, then print the thing. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

## Examples


pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases sync
pages.summary: Keep a knowledge base in step with a folder
pages.markdown:
Keep a knowledge base in step with a folder

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases sync [KB] <folder>
```

The way to keep a knowledge base matching a folder you own, such as a handbook in a repository: run it again
whenever the folder changes and only what changed is uploaded. For one file, kb documents create is simpler.

Keeps a knowledge base folder in step with a folder on disk, through one ingestion batch: every file is hashed
here, the server plans what changes (new, changed, moved, unchanged), you confirm, the files that need their bytes
are uploaded, and the CLI waits until they're processed.

Exit codes: 0 when everything is in step; 1 when some items failed; 3 when the plan has items that need a decision
(--on-conflict answers them) or a confirmation was needed with no terminal (--yes).

Recipe: https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/recipes/keep-a-folder-in-step/

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | the scope `knowledge-bases:write,files:write` |

| --- | --- |
| `<KB>` | KB. Optional. |
| `<folder>` | Folder. Required. |

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases watch
pages.markdown:
Watch a knowledge base (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases watch <kb> [flags]
```

Watches a knowledge base, or one document, folder or batch in it: a snapshot first, then each change.

Every connection starts with `snapshot`: the thing watched as it stands, its running and recently finished jobs, and the progress of each document being processed. Then one event per change. A reconnect needs no cursor, because it starts with a snapshot again; nothing is replayed and nothing is lost. The SDKs build every scope's `watch()` and `wait()` on this: `wait()` returns once no job on the thing is running, or raises the error of the job that failed. Events name a document only to callers who may read it. The server ends the stream after at most an hour, and the SDKs reconnect.

What the caller needs depends on what it watches. The whole knowledge base needs the knowledge base read permission and the files list permission, because the snapshot returns the knowledge base and the documents' progress. One document or folder needs the files list permission. One batch needs the ingestion list permission, because the snapshot returns the batch.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.read` (scope `knowledge-bases:read`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Output | A stream of events: one JSON object per event with `--output jsonl` |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).watch`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/watch-knowledge-base/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/events`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/watch-knowledge-base/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-watch.input.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases watch --format json` prints them too |

pages.summary: Who may read a knowledge base
pages.markdown:
Who may read a knowledge base

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases access <command> [flags]
```

The readers of the whole knowledge base: its top-level folder's access, which everything inherits unless given
its own.

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`caitlyn knowledge-bases access get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/knowledge-bases/access/#get) | Get access |
| [`caitlyn knowledge-bases access set`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/knowledge-bases/access/#set) | Set access |

## get

Get access (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases access get <kb> [flags]
```

Gets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

Without `folder` or `document`, the knowledge base's role grants (`roles`). With `folder`, that folder's `readers`; with `document`, that document's. `inheritedFrom` names the folder whose readers apply when they are inherited. A folder or document the caller may not see is 404. The root folder (`folder=/`, `kb.folders('/').access`) holds the readers every folder falls back to; its readers are never inherited.

For a folder or document, the `readers` also come back on ListFolders, ListDocuments and GetDocument too, with `inheritedFrom`, under the files list and read permissions. What GetAccess adds is the access on its own, with the ETag that SetAccess's `If-Match` takes, and the root folder's readers; reading it needs the files permissions list permission.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.read` (scope `knowledge-bases:read`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).access.get`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/get-access/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/access`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/get-access/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-access-get.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-access-get.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases access get --format json` prints them too |

| Flag | Type | Description |

| `--document` | string | A document in it. At most 128 characters. |
| `--folder` | string | A folder in it, for example '/hr/investigations/'. At most 1024 characters. Matches `^/([^/]+/)*$`. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh

caitlyn knowledge-bases access get KB4T7YQ2WL

# Who may read a folder
caitlyn knowledge-bases access get KB4T7YQ2WL --folder /hr/investigations/

# A folder named permissions is just a folder
```

Every error is printed on stderr with a hint of what to run next ([Exit codes](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/exit-codes/)). Each error code's page, `https://build.caitlyn.ai/errors/<CODE>/`, says what it means and what to do; [Errors](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/errors/) lists them all.

## set

Set access (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases access set <kb> [flags]
```

Sets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it the write is unconditional and the last writer wins, which is safe because the caller sends the whole list. With it, access that changed since is refused with 412.

Without `folder` or `document`, send `roles`: the roles sent become the whole list. With `folder` or `document`, send `readers`; `kind: inherit` makes it follow its folder again. The knowledge base's role grants are set only without a target, under the knowledge base's own permission, as v2's knowledge base permissions route sets them, so `roles` with `folder` or `document`, `readers` without one, and both `folder` and `document` are refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The root folder (`folder=/`) holds the readers every other folder falls back to, so `inherit` is refused there with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Applying readers to the passages a folder or document holds continues after the response; the returned access says what is set, and the knowledge base's watch shows the work.

Setting `roles` is refused in two cases, as in v2. A caller may give a role only a grant it could make itself: any other is refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. And a grant that is not safe for guests, given to a role that guests or anonymous visitors use, is refused with 422 `RBAC_NOT_GUEST_SAFE`. Only the grants being added are judged, so a grant the role already holds never blocks an unrelated change. Both checks are made by the server on the roles sent.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `user-facing`: changes what other people get; AI agents and CI pass `--yes` |
| Needs | `knowledge-bases.update` (scope `knowledge-bases:write`) and update on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).access.set`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/put-access/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`PUT /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/access`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/put-access/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-access-set.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-access-set.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases access set --format json` prints them too |

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<kb>` | The knowledge base. Required. |

### Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--document` | string | A document in it. At most 128 characters. |
| `--folder` | string | A folder in it. At most 1024 characters. Matches `^/([^/]+/)*$`. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--if-match` | string | Only if the thing still has this ETag (412 otherwise). Without it, the change applies to the thing as it is now. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

### Examples

```sh
# Only the HR team may read investigations
caitlyn knowledge-bases access set KB4T7YQ2WL --set 'readers=json:{"kind":"specific","roles":["hr-team"]}' \
    --folder /hr/investigations/ --if-match '"2"'

# A document follows its folder again, whatever its access was
caitlyn knowledge-bases access set KB4T7YQ2WL --set 'readers=json:{"kind":"inherit"}' --document doc-3b7f9e21

# Role grants sent with a folder: fails with VALIDATION_FAILED, exit code 1
caitlyn knowledge-bases access set KB4T7YQ2WL --set 'roles=json:[{"roleId":"hr-team","can":["find","read"]}]' \
    --folder /hr/

# The access changed since it was read: fails with PRECONDITION_FAILED, exit code 7
caitlyn knowledge-bases access set KB4T7YQ2WL --set 'roles=json:[]' --if-match '"3"'
```

pages.markdown:

```sh

```

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents cancel-processing
pages.markdown:
Stop processing a document (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents cancel-processing <document> [flags]
```

Stops the work running on a document: its ingestion, a fill-in or reprocessing.

A stopped first version removes the document; a stopped new version leaves the current one serving. Until stopping running work is built, every call is refused with 409 `CONFLICT` ("This document's processing can't be stopped yet"), so callers can build against it now.

Needs the files update permission. Stopping a first version removes the document, so it also needs the files delete permission, and a caller without it is refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The server checks this, because the permission trait follows input members, not the document's state.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes` |
| Needs | `files.update` (scope `files:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Long-running | Waits with `--wait` (where it starts work) and `--timeout`; AI agents get a 4-minute default and a command that resumes the wait |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).documents(documentId).cancelProcessing`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/cancel-document-processing/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents/{documentId}/cancel-processing`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/cancel-document-processing/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-cancel-processing.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-cancel-processing.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases documents cancel-processing --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

## Flags

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents cancel-processing doc-3b7f9e21 --kb KB4T7YQ2WL

# Until stopping is built: fails with CONFLICT, exit code 7
```

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents create
pages.markdown:
Add a document (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents create <file> [flags]
```

Creates a document from an upload; ingestion continues after the response.

Returns 202 with the document in its initial state and the Operation that tracks ingestion, and `Location` names the document: read it with GetDocument, or wait for it with the SDKs' `wait()`. Metadata sent here is written with the document before ingestion starts, so even the first ingestion keeps it. Needs the files permission, read access to the knowledge base and access to the folder; it does not need update access to the knowledge base, which is for the knowledge base's own configuration.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `files.create` (scope `files:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Long-running | Waits with `--wait` (where it starts work) and `--timeout`; AI agents get a 4-minute default and a command that resumes the wait |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).documents.create`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/create-document/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/create-document/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-create.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-create.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases documents create --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<file>` | The file to upload, or `-` for stdin with `--file-name`. Required. |

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--estimate` | bool | Print the estimate and send nothing else. |
| `--external-id` | string | The caller's own key for the document, unique within the knowledge base. At most 128 characters. |
| `--folder` | string, required | The folder to put the document in. At most 1024 characters. Matches `^/([^/]+/)*$`. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |

| `--name` | string | What the document is called in the knowledge base and in citations. At most 1024 characters. |
| `--progress` | bool | Print progress lines even without a terminal. |
| `--set` | string, repeatable | Set a nested member: path=value, @file reads a file, json:… parses JSON. Repeatable. |
| `--source-url` | string | The address a citation of this document links to: 'https', at most 2,048 characters. At most 2048 characters. Matches `^https://[^ ]+$`. |
| `--timeout` | string | The wait's time limit, for example 30m (exit 9 when it passes). |
| `--upload-id` | string, required | The upload holding the document's bytes. At most 128 characters. |
| `--wait` | bool | Wait until the work it starts has finished, then print the thing. |

And the [global flags](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/reference/#global-flags).

```sh
# Add an uploaded file to the HR folder
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents create --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --source-url https://intranet.harbourfreight.example/hr/leave-policy \
    --external-id hr/leave-policy --set 'metadata=json:{"title":"Leave policy","policyOwner":"hr"}' \
    --upload-id 0193a6f2-1111-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 --folder /hr/ --name 'Leave policy' ./file.pdf

caitlyn knowledge-bases documents create --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --upload-id 0193a6f2-1111-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 \
    --folder /hr/ ./file.pdf

# A metadata field the knowledge base does not define: fails with METADATA_FIELD_UNDEFINED, exit code 1
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents create --kb KB4T7YQ2WL --set 'metadata=json:{"policyOwnr":"hr"}' \
    --upload-id 0193a6f2-1111-7a2b-8c3d-4e5f60718293 --folder /hr/ ./file.pdf
```

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents delete
pages.markdown:
Delete a document (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents delete <document> [flags]
```

Deletes a document; removing it from search continues after the response.

Returns 202 with the document in `deleting`; in the SDKs, `.wait()` on the result waits until it is gone. Repeating the call while the document is still `deleting` returns 202 again; once it is gone, 404, as for any record that does not exist.

A document still being processed (`pending` or `processing`) is deleted too: its processing stops, and it does not come back.

Needs the files delete permission, read access to the knowledge base and access to the document's folder.

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents delete-many
pages.markdown:
Delete many documents (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents delete-many [flags]
```

Deletes up to 100 documents in one call, with a result for each.

Each document is deleted as DeleteDocument deletes one. The call returns 200 even when every item fails: `results` has one entry per identifier, always in request order, each either `accepted` (the document is now `deleting`, or already was) or `failed` with a code: `NOT_FOUND` for a document that is gone or that the caller may not see, or `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when it could not be marked for deletion; try that one again. A document still being processed is deleted like any other. One failed item never stops the others. More than 100 identifiers, none, or the same identifier twice is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` for the whole call. Safe to repeat: a repeat gives the same results, apart from `NOT_FOUND` for documents that finished deleting in between.

| --- | --- |
| Impact | `destructive`: can't be undone; asks first, and AI agents and CI pass `--yes` |
| Needs | `files.delete` (scope `files:admin`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents download
pages.summary: Save a document's bytes to a file
pages.markdown:
Save a document's bytes to a file (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents download <document> [flags]
```

Saves the document to a file: by default its own name, in the current folder, and never over an existing file
without --force. --out - writes it to stdout, but not to a terminal unless it is text. --url-only prints the
short-lived address of the bytes and when it expires instead, as -o json, yaml or jsonl does without --out; -o
is always the output format, never a file.

Needs:
  files.read (scope files:read) and read on the knowledge base.
  Returns 404 when it isn't shared with you. People and API clients.

Impact: Reads only.

When it fails:
  404 NOT_FOUND                A document that does not exist, or that the caller may not see.  Exit code 6.

Available from Caitlyn 5.149.0.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `files.read` (scope `files:read`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).documents(documentId).download`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/get-document-download/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents/{documentId}/download`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/get-document-download/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-download.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-download.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases documents download --format json` prints them too |

| `--force` | bool | Overwrite the file if it exists. |

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents list
pages.markdown:
List documents (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents list [flags]
```

Lists the documents in a knowledge base, one page at a time.

Documents are returned in a stable order that does not change between pages. Filters combine with AND, and an unknown filter is refused with 400 `UNKNOWN_FILTER`. With `filter[folder][eq]`, the documents directly in that folder; with `deep` as well, every document below it. `q` keeps documents whose name contains the text. The list can be sorted by `folder`, `name`, `updatedAt` (when the document last changed) and `byteSize`. With no `sort`, documents come by folder, then name.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `read`: reads only |
| Needs | `files.list` (scope `files:read`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).documents.list`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/list-documents/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`GET /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/list-documents/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-list.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-list.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases documents list --format json` prints them too |

| `--folder` | string | Only documents directly in this folder, or below it with 'deep'. At most 1024 characters. Matches `^/([^/]+/)*$`. |

pages.title: caitlyn knowledge-bases documents replace
pages.markdown:
Replace a document's file (beta)

```sh
caitlyn knowledge-bases documents replace <document> <file> [flags]
```

Adds new bytes to a document as a new version; ingestion continues after the response.

The new version becomes the current one once it is indexed; until then the current version keeps serving search. The bytes must be the same file type as the document's: another type is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, because a new type is a new document. While a version is still processing, another is refused with 409 `DOCUMENT_INGESTION_IN_PROGRESS` and `Retry-After`. Bytes the same as the current version's make no new version (`result: unchanged`); bytes the same as an earlier version's bring that version back (`result: restored`).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Impact | `write`: changes drafts or your own work |
| Needs | `files.update` (scope `files:write`) and read on the knowledge base; returns 404 when it isn't shared with you |
| Who can run it | People and API clients |
| Stability | Beta: it may change before it is generally available |
| Since | Caitlyn 5.149.0 |
| Long-running | Waits with `--wait` (where it starts work) and `--timeout`; AI agents get a 4-minute default and a command that resumes the wait |
| In the SDKs | [`caitlyn.knowledgeBases(knowledgeBaseId).documents(documentId).replace`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/sdk/create-document-version/) |
| In the HTTP API | [`POST /api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents/{documentId}/versions`](https://build.caitlyn.ai/api/create-document-version/) |
| JSON Schema | [input](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-replace.input.json) and [output](https://build.caitlyn.ai/cli/schemas/knowledge-bases-documents-replace.output.json); `caitlyn help knowledge-bases documents replace --format json` prints them too |

## Arguments

| --- | --- |
| `<document>` | The document. Required. |
| `<file>` | The file to upload, or `-` for stdin with `--file-name`. Required. |

## Flags

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--estimate` | bool | Print the estimate and send nothing else. |
| `-f`, `--from-file` | string | The whole input from a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Flags override it. |
| `--generate-input` | bool | Print an input skeleton (YAML) with every member and its documentation. |
| `--idempotency-key` | string | Reuse this key when re-running the same command (default: a new key per run). |
